## Lab 5.1 — Refactor existing tests into the Page Object Model 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Explain the **Page Object Model (POM)** and its three parts: locators, actions, checks.
* Write a **base class** that every page shares, and small **components** for repeated page parts.
* Refactor the Sign-in tests of Lab 3.3 into page objects without changing what they check.

### Concepts in simple language

A **Page Object** is a class that represents **one page** (or one part of a page) of the application. It is the only place that knows *how* the page is built.

```
BEFORE (in the test)                                  AFTER (in the test)
await page.getByLabel('Username').fill(u);            await loginPage.submit(u, p);
await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(p);
await page.getByRole('button', {name:'Sign in'})
          .click();
```

A page object has three kinds of members:

| Kind | Example | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Locators** (properties) | `usernameInput`, `signInButton` | `readonly`, created once in the constructor; **public**, so a test may use them for a one-off check |
| **Actions** (methods that do something) | `submit(user, pass)`, `registerAs(user)` | Named for what the *user* does (`signIn`), not for what the browser does (`clickButton`) |
| **Checks** (methods that look) | `expectLoaded()`, `expectFormError(text)` | Named `expectSomething`. They take the **expected value from the test** — the page object does not decide what is correct |

**Inheritance and composition.** All pages share a few things: they hold the Playwright `page`, they know their address, they can be opened, and they have the top bar. Put that in one **base class** (`BasePage`) and let each page `extend` it. Parts that appear on many pages — the top bar, the notification message — become small **components** that the base class *has* (composition): `this.header`, `this.notice`.

**TypeScript you need (all from Phase 2):**

| Syntax | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| `class LoginPage extends BasePage` | A `LoginPage` *is a* `BasePage` and gets everything it has |
| `abstract class BasePage` | A class that is never created directly; it demands that children fill in the gaps |
| `abstract readonly path: string` | Every child **must** say what its address is |
| `constructor(protected readonly page: Page)` | Receive the `page` and store it; `protected` = visible to the class and its children |
| `async expectLoaded(): Promise<void>` | An asynchronous method that returns nothing; always `await` it |

### Why QA needs it

* **Maintenance:** the application changes, you edit **one** file.
* **Readability:** a test reads as a user story; a reviewer can check it against the requirement.
* **Reuse:** the second test that needs the Sign-in page costs one line.

### Prerequisites

Lab 5.0 (folders exist), Phase 2 Lab 2.5 (classes), Phase 3 Lab 3.3 (the Sign-in tests).

### Files

```
pages/base-page.ts                    NEW  what every page shares
pages/components/header.ts            NEW  the top bar (who am I, sign out)
pages/components/notice.ts            NEW  the status message
pages/login-page.ts                   NEW  the Sign in page
pages/register-page.ts                NEW  the Create account page
tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts       NEW  the Sign-in tests, refactored
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the components.** A component is a mini page object for a piece that many pages show. Create `pages/components/header.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/components/header.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * COMPONENT: the top bar that every signed-in page has.
 * A component is a small page object for a piece of the page that appears on MANY pages,
 * so its locators are written once.
 */
export class Header {
  readonly whoami: Locator;
  readonly signOutButton: Locator;
  readonly brandLink: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.whoami = page.locator('#whoami');
    this.signOutButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign out' });
    this.brandLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Book Library' });
  }

  async expectSignedInAs(username: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.whoami).toHaveText(`Signed in as ${username}`);
  }

  async signOut(): Promise<void> {
    await this.signOutButton.click();
  }
}
```

and `pages/components/notice.ts` (the green message after an action, or the banner on the Sign-in page — both have `role="status"`):

*File: `e2e/pages/components/notice.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * COMPONENT: the short message that tells the user what just happened.
 * On the Books pages it is the "toast" (it disappears after about 4 seconds);
 * on the Sign-in page it is a banner. Both have role="status", so one locator serves both.
 */
export class Notice {
  readonly area: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.area = page.getByRole('status');
  }

  async expectMessage(text: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.area).toHaveText(text);
  }
}
```

**Step 2 — the base class.** Create `pages/base-page.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/base-page.ts`*

```ts
import { type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { Header } from './components/header';
import { Notice } from './components/notice';

/**
 * The parent of every page object. It holds what ALL pages share:
 * the browser page, the components, and the "open this page" behaviour.
 */
export abstract class BasePage {
  readonly header: Header;
  readonly notice: Notice;

  /** The address of the page, relative to baseURL (for example "/login/"). */
  abstract readonly path: string;

  constructor(protected readonly page: Page) {
    this.header = new Header(page);
    this.notice = new Notice(page);
  }

  /** Every page object must say how to recognise that its page has finished loading. */
  abstract expectLoaded(): Promise<void>;

  /** Go to the page and wait until it is really there. */
  async open(): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.goto(this.path);
    await this.expectLoaded();
  }
}
```

**Step 3 — the Sign-in page.** Create `pages/login-page.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/login-page.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';
import { BasePage } from './base-page';

export class LoginPage extends BasePage {
  readonly path = '/login/';

  readonly heading: Locator;
  readonly usernameInput: Locator;
  readonly passwordInput: Locator;
  readonly signInButton: Locator;
  readonly formError: Locator;
  readonly usernameError: Locator;
  readonly passwordError: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.heading = page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Sign in' });
    this.usernameInput = page.getByLabel('Username');
    this.passwordInput = page.getByLabel('Password');
    this.signInButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' });
    this.formError = page.getByRole('alert');
    this.usernameError = page.locator('#username-error');
    this.passwordError = page.locator('#password-error');
  }

  async expectLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.heading).toBeVisible();
  }

  /** Fill the two fields and press the button. Does NOT check what happens next. */
  async submit(username: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.usernameInput.fill(username);
    await this.passwordInput.fill(password);
    await this.signInButton.click();
  }

  /** Sign in with a user object. (In Lab 5.3 this will hand back the next page.) */
  async signIn(user: TestUser): Promise<void> {
    await this.submit(user.username, user.password);
  }

  async expectOnThisPage(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/\/login\//);
  }

  async expectFormError(message: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.formError).toHaveText(message);
  }
}
```

**Step 4 — the Create-account page.** Create `pages/register-page.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/register-page.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';
import { BasePage } from './base-page';

export class RegisterPage extends BasePage {
  readonly path = '/register/';

  readonly heading: Locator;
  readonly usernameInput: Locator;
  readonly passwordInput: Locator;
  readonly createButton: Locator;
  readonly usernameError: Locator;
  readonly passwordError: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.heading = page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Create an account' });
    this.usernameInput = page.getByLabel('Username');
    this.passwordInput = page.getByLabel('Password');
    this.createButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' });
    this.usernameError = page.locator('#username-error');
    this.passwordError = page.locator('#password-error');
  }

  async expectLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.heading).toBeVisible();
  }

  async fill(username: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.usernameInput.fill(username);
    await this.passwordInput.fill(password);
  }

  /** Create the account. The site then sends the user to the Sign-in page. */
  async registerAs(user: TestUser): Promise<void> {
    await this.fill(user.username, user.password);
    await this.createButton.click();
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/\/login\/$/);
  }
}
```

**Step 5 — the refactored tests.** Compare with `tests/02-login.spec.ts` from Lab 3.3 — the same three scenarios, plus a fourth that we get nearly for free. Create `tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { LoginPage } from '../../pages/login-page';
import { RegisterPage } from '../../pages/register-page';
import { newUser } from '../../utils/ui-steps';

test.describe('Sign in', () => {
  test('a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page', async ({ page }) => {
    const user = newUser('anna');
    const registerPage = new RegisterPage(page);
    await registerPage.open(); // arrange: the account must exist
    await registerPage.registerAs(user);

    const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
    await loginPage.signIn(user); // act

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/); // assert
    await loginPage.header.expectSignedInAs(user.username);
  });

  test('a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page', async ({ page }) => {
    const user = newUser();
    const registerPage = new RegisterPage(page);
    await registerPage.open();
    await registerPage.registerAs(user);

    const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
    await loginPage.submit(user.username, 'not-the-password');

    await loginPage.expectFormError('Invalid username or password.');
    await loginPage.expectOnThisPage();
  });

  test('an unknown user is rejected with the same message', async ({ page }) => {
    const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit('nobody_' + Date.now(), 'whatever-123');

    await loginPage.expectFormError('Invalid username or password.');
  });

  test('both fields are required', async ({ page }) => {
    const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.signInButton.click();

    await expect(loginPage.usernameError).toHaveText('Username is required.');
    await expect(loginPage.passwordError).toHaveText('Password is required.');
  });
});
```

**Step 6 — type-check and run.**

```powershell
npm run typecheck
npx playwright test tests/framework --project=chromium
```

### Expected output

```text

Running 4 tests using 1 worker

  ✓  1 [chromium] › tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts:7:7 › Sign in › a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page (1.4s)
  ✓  2 [chromium] › tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts:20:7 › Sign in › a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page (1.1s)
  ✓  3 [chromium] › tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts:33:7 › Sign in › an unknown user is rejected with the same message (683ms)
  ✓  4 [chromium] › tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts:41:7 › Sign in › both fields are required (391ms)

  4 passed (4.4s)
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `export class Header` | A component: a plain class that holds locators; it is not a `BasePage` because it has no address |
| `constructor(page: Page)` | Components receive the Playwright `page` and build their locators |
| `this.whoami = page.locator('#whoami')` | The one place that knows how to find "Signed in as …" |
| `async expectSignedInAs(username)` | A **check**: the test passes the expected name, the component compares |
| `export abstract class BasePage` | Cannot be created with `new`; exists to be extended |
| `abstract readonly path: string` | Each page must declare its address |
| `abstract expectLoaded()` | Each page must define what "finished loading" means for *it* (usually "its heading is visible") |
| `async open()` | Shared behaviour: go to the page, then wait until it is really there. No test ever needs `page.goto('/login/')` again |
| `readonly path = '/login/'` | The child fills in the abstract member |
| `super(page)` | Call the parent's constructor first (it creates `header` and `notice`) |
| `submit(username, password)` | An **action**: fill both fields and press the button. It does **not** check the result, because other tests expect other results |
| `registerAs(user)` | Fills the form, presses the button, and then checks the one thing that *must* be true after a successful registration: the address is the Sign-in page |
| `new LoginPage(page)` in a test | The page object is created **inside** the test, where `page` exists. Never at the top of the file |
| `loginPage.expectFormError('…')` | The text is passed in **by the test**, so the requirement stays visible in the test |

### What changed — before and after

| Measure | `tests/02-login.spec.ts` (Phase 3) | `tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| Raw locator calls in the test file | many | **none** (the one `signInButton.click()` uses a locator the page object owns) |
| Places that know the name of the Sign-in button | every test file that signs in | `login-page.ts` only |
| Lines needed to sign in | 4 | 1 (`signIn`) |

### Try it: one change, one fix

Prove the benefit yourself. In `pages/login-page.ts` change the button's name from `'Sign in'` to `'Log in'`, as if the product team had renamed it, and run the Sign-in tests with a short timeout:

```powershell
npx playwright test tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts --project=chromium --timeout=5000
```

Four tests fail — and the first lines of every failure point to the **same file and line**. This is what you will see for the first one (shortened):

```text
  1) [chromium] › tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts:7:7 › Sign in › a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page 

    Test timeout of 5000ms exceeded.

    Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 5000ms exceeded.
    Call log:
```

Change `'Log in'` back to `'Sign in'` (one edit!), and all four pass again. With copy-pasted locators you would have edited every file.

### Common mistakes

* **Putting the decision in the page object.** `async expectInvalidLogin()` that hard-codes `'Invalid username or password.'` hides the requirement from the test. Pass the text in from the test, or (Lab 5.5) from one shared list of messages.
* **A "god" page object** with 80 methods for the whole application. One class per page, components for shared parts.
* **Creating a page object outside the test** (`const loginPage = new LoginPage(page)` at the top of the file) — `page` does not exist there.
* **Forgetting `await`** on an action: the test races ahead of the browser. Every method that returns `Promise<…>` needs `await`.
* **Methods named after the mechanism** (`clickSignInButton`) instead of the intention (`signIn`). The mechanism may change; the intention does not.
* **Making every locator `private`.** Keep them public: a test may legitimately need `loginPage.signInButton` for one special check.

### Troubleshooting

Real compiler messages from mistakes you may make. (`npm run typecheck` shows them; the editor underlines them as you type.)

```text
pages/broken-demo.ts(3,14): error TS2515: Non-abstract class 'HalfPage' does not implement inherited abstract member expectLoaded from class 'BasePage'.
pages/broken-demo.ts(8,21): error TS2511: Cannot create an instance of an abstract class.
tests/framework/zz-typo.spec.ts(7,19): error TS2551: Property 'signInn' does not exist on type 'LoginPage'. Did you mean 'signIn'?
tests/framework/zz-typo.spec.ts(8,35): error TS2561: Object literal may only specify known properties, but 'tiemout' does not exist in type '{ … }'. Did you mean to write 'timeout'?
```

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `TS2515 Non-abstract class 'HalfPage' does not implement inherited abstract member expectLoaded` | A child page forgot a member the base class demands | Write `expectLoaded()` in the child |
| `TS2511 Cannot create an instance of an abstract class` | `new BasePage(...)` | Create a concrete child (`new LoginPage(page)`) |
| `TS2551 Property 'signInn' does not exist … Did you mean 'signIn'?` | A typo in a method name | Use the suggestion. This is a benefit of TypeScript: the typo is found **before** the run |
| `TS2561 Object literal may only specify known properties … Did you mean to write 'timeout'?` | A typo in an option name | Same: read the last sentence of the message |
| Tests time out waiting for a button | The locator in the page object does not match the page | Fix it **once**, in the page object (see *Try it*) |

```ts
// 1  in LoginPage
readonly createAccountLink: Locator;                   // constructor: page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Create an account' })
async goToCreateAccount(): Promise<void> {

}
// test
test('the Sign in page links to Create account', async ({ page }) => {

  await new RegisterPage(page).expectLoaded();

// 2
test('the button stays disabled until both fields are filled', async ({ page }) => {

  await registerPage.open();
```

3. The raw locator puts knowledge of the page in the test, so the next change to that field has to be fixed in every test that copied it. Use `loginPage.usernameInput.fill('x')` (a public locator of the page object) or add an action to the page object if several tests need it.

1. What are the three kinds of members of a page object? *(Locators, actions, checks.)*
2. Why is `BasePage` abstract? *(It is never used alone; it forces each page to declare its `path` and `expectLoaded()`.)*

## Lab 5.2 — The dashboard: `BooksPage`, `BookFormPage` and a reusable component 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Create the page objects for the **Books** page (the application's dashboard) and the **Add/Edit book** form.
* Write **reusable methods**: find one book's row, delete a book, check a row's details.
* Create a **component** for the Delete confirmation dialog.
* Keep **locators out of the tests**.

### Concepts in simple language

A good page object offers three levels of help:

| Level | Example | When a test uses it |
|---|---|---|
| **Locators** | `booksPage.rows`, `booksPage.searchBox` | A one-off check |
| **Queries** that build a locator for a particular thing | `booksPage.rowFor('PW Book 3fa9')` | "That book's row" |
| **User actions** | `booksPage.deleteBook(title)`, `bookFormPage.save(book)` | The normal case |

**Reusable methods hide the boring, fragile parts.** `rowFor(title)` encodes what you learned in Labs 3.8 and 4.0: the library is shared, so find a row by a link with the **exact** title (`exact: true`; otherwise the *Edit …* link also matches). Write it once; every test benefits.

**Two ways to make a form page work for both modes.** The Add and Edit forms are one page in two modes. The class does not care: it types into the same three fields. The only difference is the heading and the button text, and `Save` / `Save changes` is covered by the pattern `/^Save/`.

**A waiting rule you will meet here.** The Edit form appears first and fills its fields a moment later (it loads the book from the server). If a test types before the fields are filled, the late arrival **overwrites** the typed text. A page object is the right place to solve this once: the method that opens the Edit form waits until the Title field has the book's title.

### Why QA needs it

The Books page is where most UI tests start and end. If its details are scattered, every new feature test re-invents them. A well-built `BooksPage` makes the *next* hundred tests cheap and uniform.

### Prerequisites

Lab 5.1.

### Files

```
pages/components/confirm-dialog.ts      NEW  the "Delete book?" dialog
pages/books-page.ts                     NEW  the dashboard
pages/book-form-page.ts                 NEW  Add book / Edit book
pages/index.ts                          NEW  one import line for all page objects
tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts      NEW  add, edit, delete — through page objects
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the dialog component.** The Delete dialog is a native `<dialog>` (Lab 4.3). Create `pages/components/confirm-dialog.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/components/confirm-dialog.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

/** COMPONENT: the "Delete book?" dialog (a native <dialog>). */
export class ConfirmDialog {
  readonly root: Locator;
  readonly message: Locator;
  readonly confirmButton: Locator;
  readonly cancelButton: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    this.root = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Delete book?' });
    this.message = this.root.locator('#confirm-text');
    this.confirmButton = this.root.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' });
    this.cancelButton = this.root.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' });
  }

  async expectAbout(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.root).toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.message).toContainText(title);
  }

  async confirm(): Promise<void> {
    await this.confirmButton.click();
    await expect(this.root).toBeHidden();
  }

  async cancel(): Promise<void> {
    await this.cancelButton.click();
    await expect(this.root).toBeHidden();
  }
}
```

**Step 2 — the form page.** Create `pages/book-form-page.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/book-form-page.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { BookData } from '../utils/types';
import { BasePage } from './base-page';
import { BooksPage } from './books-page';

/** What a test gives the form. The year may be a number, text (to try invalid input) or missing. */
export type BookInput = Pick<BookData, 'title' | 'author'> & { published_year?: number | string | null };

/** What the form's three message areas should say. Leave a field out to say "no message needed". */
export interface FormErrors {
  title?: string;
  author?: string;
  year?: string;
}

/** The Add book / Edit book form (same page, two modes). */
export class BookFormPage extends BasePage {
  readonly path = '/books/new/';

  readonly titleInput: Locator;
  readonly authorInput: Locator;
  readonly yearInput: Locator;
  readonly saveButton: Locator;
  readonly cancelLink: Locator;
  readonly heading: Locator;
  private readonly titleError: Locator;
  private readonly authorError: Locator;
  private readonly yearError: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.heading = page.getByRole('heading', { name: /^(Add|Edit) book$/ });
    this.titleInput = page.getByLabel('Title');
    this.authorInput = page.getByLabel('Author');
    this.yearInput = page.getByLabel('Published year');
    this.saveButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /^Save/ }); // "Save book" or "Save changes"
    this.cancelLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Cancel' });
    this.titleError = page.locator('#title-error');
    this.authorError = page.locator('#author-error');
    this.yearError = page.locator('#year-error');
  }

  async expectLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.heading).toBeVisible();
  }

  /** Type into the three fields. A null year leaves the field empty. */
  async fill(book: BookInput): Promise<void> {
    await this.titleInput.fill(book.title);
    await this.authorInput.fill(book.author);
    await this.yearInput.fill(book.published_year == null ? '' : String(book.published_year));
  }

  /** Press Save and do not assume it worked (use it for invalid data). */
  async submit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.saveButton.click();
  }

  /** The happy path: fill, save, and hand back the Books page. */
  async save(book: BookInput): Promise<BooksPage> {
    await this.fill(book);
    await this.submit();
    const books = new BooksPage(this.page);
    await books.expectLoaded();
    return books;
  }

  async expectErrors(errors: FormErrors): Promise<void> {
    await this.expectMessage(this.titleError, errors.title);
    await this.expectMessage(this.authorError, errors.author);
    await this.expectMessage(this.yearError, errors.year);
  }

  private async expectMessage(area: Locator, text: string | undefined): Promise<void> {
    if (text === undefined) await expect(area).toBeHidden();
    else await expect(area).toHaveText(text);
  }

  /** Edit mode: wait until the application has loaded the book into the Title field. */
  async expectPrefilledWith(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.titleInput).toHaveValue(title);
  }

  async expectStillOnForm(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/new\/$|\/edit\/$/);
  }
}
```

**Step 3 — the dashboard.** Create `pages/books-page.ts`:

*File: `e2e/pages/books-page.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { BasePage } from './base-page';
import { BookFormPage } from './book-form-page';
import { LoginPage } from './login-page';
import { ConfirmDialog } from './components/confirm-dialog';

/** The values of the "Sort by" list (what the application sends as ordering=...). */
export type SortOrder = '-id' | 'title' | '-title' | 'published_year' | '-published_year';

/**
 * The Books page. After signing in this is the "dashboard" of the Book Library:
 * the page every signed-in user lands on.
 */
export class BooksPage extends BasePage {
  readonly path = '/books/';

  readonly heading: Locator;
  readonly searchBox: Locator;
  readonly sortList: Locator;
  readonly addBookLink: Locator;
  readonly rows: Locator;
  readonly countText: Locator;
  readonly emptyMessage: Locator;
  readonly confirmDialog: ConfirmDialog;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.heading = page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Books' });
    this.searchBox = page.getByLabel('Search books');
    this.sortList = page.getByLabel('Sort by');
    this.addBookLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Add book' });
    this.rows = page.getByTestId('book-row');
    this.countText = page.locator('#count');
    this.emptyMessage = page.locator('#empty');
    this.confirmDialog = new ConfirmDialog(page);
  }

  async expectLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.heading).toBeVisible();
  }

  // ---- finding things ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  /** The row that contains a link with exactly this title. The library is shared, so match exactly. */
  rowFor(title: string): Locator {
    return this.rows.filter({ has: this.page.getByRole('link', { name: title, exact: true }) });
  }

  // ---- actions (they return the next page when the user lands on another one) -------------

  async goToAddBook(): Promise<BookFormPage> {
    await this.addBookLink.click();
    const form = new BookFormPage(this.page);
    await form.expectLoaded();
    return form;
  }

  async goToEditBook(title: string): Promise<BookFormPage> {
    await this.page.getByRole('link', { name: `Edit ${title}`, exact: true }).click();
    const form = new BookFormPage(this.page);
    await form.expectLoaded();
    await form.expectPrefilledWith(title); // the form fills itself AFTER it appears: do not type before that
    return form;
  }

  async search(text: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.searchBox.fill(text);
  }

  async sortBy(order: SortOrder): Promise<void> {
    await this.sortList.selectOption(order);
  }

  /** Delete a book and confirm in the dialog. */
  async deleteBook(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: `Delete ${title}`, exact: true }).click();
    await this.confirmDialog.expectAbout(title);
    await this.confirmDialog.confirm();
  }

  async startDeleting(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: `Delete ${title}`, exact: true }).click();
    await this.confirmDialog.expectAbout(title);
  }

  async signOut(): Promise<LoginPage> {
    await this.header.signOut();
    const login = new LoginPage(this.page);
    await login.expectLoaded();
    return login;
  }

  // ---- checks ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  async expectBook(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.rowFor(title)).toHaveCount(1);
  }

  async expectNoBook(title: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.rowFor(title)).toHaveCount(0);
  }

  /** Check the columns of one row: author, year ("—" when missing) and owner. */
  async expectRow(title: string, expected: { author: string; year: string; owner: string }): Promise<void> {
    const cells = this.rowFor(title).getByRole('cell');
    await expect(cells).toHaveCount(5);
    await expect(cells.nth(1)).toHaveText(expected.author);
    await expect(cells.nth(2)).toHaveText(expected.year);
    await expect(cells.nth(3)).toHaveText(expected.owner);
  }

  async expectOwnerControls(title: string, visible: boolean): Promise<void> {
    const edit = this.page.getByRole('link', { name: `Edit ${title}`, exact: true });
    const del = this.page.getByRole('button', { name: `Delete ${title}`, exact: true });
    if (visible) {
      await expect(edit).toBeVisible();
      await expect(del).toBeVisible();
    } else {
      await expect(edit).toHaveCount(0);
      await expect(del).toHaveCount(0);
    }
  }

  /** Wait until the titles on screen are exactly these, in this order (retries, so it waits for the list). */
  async expectTitlesInOrder(titles: string[]): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.rows.locator('td:nth-child(1)')).toHaveText(titles);
  }

  /** The titles on screen, in order. Call it after an assertion proved the list has settled. */
  async titles(): Promise<string[]> {
    return this.rows.locator('td:nth-child(1)').allTextContents();
  }
}
```

**Step 5 — the tests.** Sign-in is still done by the old helper `createUserAndSignIn` for now (Lab 5.4 replaces it); everything else goes through the page objects. Create `tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import { BooksPage } from '../../pages';
import { createUserAndSignIn } from '../../utils/ui-steps';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';

test.describe('Books: add, edit, delete', () => {
  test('an added book appears in the list with its details', async ({ page }) => {
    const user = await createUserAndSignIn(page); // the old helper still does the sign-in
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: 1984 });

    const booksPage = new BooksPage(page); // ...and now we can talk to the page through its object
    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    const books = await form.save(book);

    await books.notice.expectMessage('Book added.');
    await books.expectRow(book.title, { author: book.author, year: '1984', owner: user.username });
  });

  test('the year is optional: a book without one shows a dash', async ({ page }) => {
    const user = await createUserAndSignIn(page);
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: null });

    const form = await new BooksPage(page).goToAddBook();
    const books = await form.save(book);

    await books.expectRow(book.title, { author: book.author, year: '—', owner: user.username });
  });

  test('editing a book changes its title', async ({ page }) => {
    await createUserAndSignIn(page);
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await new BooksPage(page).goToAddBook()).save(book);

    const form = await books.goToEditBook(book.title);
    const newTitle = `${book.title} (2nd ed.)`;
    const updated = await form.save({ ...book, title: newTitle });

    await updated.notice.expectMessage('Book updated.');
    await updated.expectBook(newTitle);
    await updated.expectNoBook(book.title);
  });

  test('deleting a book removes it after the user confirms', async ({ page }) => {
    await createUserAndSignIn(page);
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await new BooksPage(page).goToAddBook()).save(book);

    await books.deleteBook(book.title);

    await books.notice.expectMessage('Book deleted.');
    await books.expectNoBook(book.title);
  });

  test('cancelling the delete dialog keeps the book', async ({ page }) => {
    await createUserAndSignIn(page);
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await new BooksPage(page).goToAddBook()).save(book);

    await books.startDeleting(book.title);
    await books.confirmDialog.cancel();

    await books.expectBook(book.title);
  });
});
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `export type SortOrder = '-id' \| 'title' \| …` | A **union of literal types**: `sortBy('titel')` is a compile error. The type documents the allowed values |
| `readonly rows = page.getByTestId('book-row')` | The row locator, defined once |
| `rowFor(title)` | `this.rows.filter({ has: link(title, exact) })` — the row **containing** a link with exactly that title |
| `goToAddBook(): Promise<BookFormPage>` | The action returns the page the user lands on (Lab 5.3 explains why) |
| `goToEditBook` … `expectPrefilledWith(title)` | Waits for the form to fill itself before the test types. **This is the late-fill rule** |
| `deleteBook(title)` | Click the row's *Delete …* button, check the dialog names the book, confirm, wait for it to close |
| `startDeleting(title)` | The first half of `deleteBook`, for the *Cancel* test |
| `expectRow(title, {author, year, owner})` | Checks three cells; `year` is a **string** because the empty year shows `—` |
| `expectOwnerControls(title, visible)` | One method for both "visible" and "not there", chosen by the argument |
| `expectTitlesInOrder([...])` | `toHaveText([...])` on the title cells: it **retries** until the list has settled (a plain `titles()` reading does not) |
| `fill(book: BookInput)` | `BookInput` allows the year to be a number, text (to try invalid input) or `null` |
| `published_year == null ? '' : String(...)` | Both `null` and `undefined` become an empty field |
| `save(book)` | The happy path: fill, submit, wait for the Books page, return it |
| `submit()` | Only presses Save; used when the data is invalid and nothing should be assumed |
| `expectErrors({ title?, author?, year? })` | A field you leave out is expected to show **no** message |
| `private async expectMessage(area, text)` | A helper only this class may use |
| Barrel `export { BooksPage, type SortOrder }` | `type` marks a name that exists only at compile time |

### Which layer owns what?

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| "Is the row for this title on the screen?" | `BooksPage.expectBook(title)` — the page object *looks*; the test decides that it *should* be there |
| "The message after adding a book is `Book added.`" | The **test** (Lab 5.5 moves the text to `data/messages.ts`) |
| "How do I find the Delete button of a book?" | `BooksPage` |

### Common mistakes

* **Returning `Locator`s from methods that should act** (or the reverse). Keep the three kinds apart: queries return locators, actions return pages or nothing, checks return nothing.
* **`first()` instead of `rowFor(title)`.** The library is shared; the first row may belong to somebody else.
* **Typing into the Edit form before it is filled** (see *Concepts*). Symptom: the typed text is silently replaced by the old value.
* **Reading `count()` or `allTextContents()` right after an action** and asserting on it. Use a checking method that retries (`expectBook`, `expectTitlesInOrder`).
* **Importing `BooksPage` from five different file paths.** Use the barrel: `import { BooksPage } from '../../pages'`.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom (real) | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `expect(locator).toHaveCount(expected) failed … Expected: 1 Received: 0` for the **new** title after an edit | Typed before the form filled itself; the late fill replaced it | Wait in the page object: `expectPrefilledWith(title)` |
| `strict mode violation: getByRole('link', …) resolved to 2 elements` | Title link and `Edit <title>` link both match | `exact: true` |
| `Cannot find module '../../pages'` | `pages/index.ts` is missing or misnamed | Create it exactly as in Step 4 |
| `TS2322 Type '"titel"' is not assignable to type 'SortOrder'` | A typo in a sort value | Use one of the five allowed values |

2. Add a method `expectEmptyListMessage(text)` to `BooksPage` and use it in a test that searches for something that does not exist. Which file contains the **text** — the page object or the test?

1. What does `rowFor(title)` encode that a beginner would forget? *(The library is shared and links overlap: find the row by a link with the exact title.)*
2. Why does `goToEditBook` end with `expectPrefilledWith`? *(The form fills itself after it appears; typing earlier would be overwritten.)*
3. Why is `year` a string in `expectRow`? *(A missing year displays `—`, not a number.)*

5. Which one is the dashboard of the Book Library? *(The Books page — `BooksPage`.)*

## Lab 5.3 — Reusable navigation methods 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Make actions **return the page object of the page the user lands on**.
* Chain a whole user journey in a few readable lines.
* Test redirects and the `?next=` behaviour through page objects.
* Understand why two page objects may import each other.

### Concepts in simple language

When a user clicks *Sign in*, a **different page** appears. If `signIn()` returns a `BooksPage`, the test cannot forget to use the right page object — the compiler hands it over:

```ts
const booksPage = await loginPage.signInAs(user);   // Sign in  -> Books
const formPage  = await booksPage.goToAddBook();    // Books    -> Add book
const back      = await formPage.save(book);        // Add book -> Books
```

This style is called **fluent navigation**. Rules:

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| A method that **moves the user** returns the next page object | The compiler guides the next step |
| The method **waits** until the next page is ready (`expectLoaded`) | The test cannot race ahead |
| Methods that stay on the same page return nothing (`Promise<void>`) | No false promises |
| Name them `goToX`, `openX`, `signInAs`, `registerAs`, `signOut` — verbs the user would say | Reads like the manual |
| Methods only know **where they lead**, not where the test should go next | The test remains the author of the story |

**Do two pages importing each other cause trouble?** `LoginPage` returns a `BooksPage`; `BooksPage.signOut()` returns a `LoginPage`. That is a circular import. It works because each file uses the other's class only **inside a method**, at the time the method runs, not while the file is being loaded. The danger is a class used at the top level (`class A extends B` where `B` is in a file that imports `A`). Keep `extends` pointing at the base class only, and circles between sibling pages are fine.

### Why QA needs it

Journeys (register → sign in → add → search → sign out) are the heart of end-to-end tests. When each step returns the next page, journeys are one-glance readable and the compiler stops you from calling `goToAddBook()` on the wrong page.

### Prerequisites

Lab 5.2.

```
pages/login-page.ts                      CHANGED  signInAs() returns BooksPage
pages/register-page.ts                   CHANGED  registerAs() returns LoginPage
tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts          CHANGED  uses the returned pages
tests/framework/navigation.spec.ts       NEW  journeys, redirects, Cancel, the logo link
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — `LoginPage.signInAs`.** Replace `pages/login-page.ts` with this version. Three things changed: `import { BooksPage }`, `signIn` became `signInAs` and returns the page, and a link locator for the exercise was added.

*File: `e2e/pages/login-page.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';
import { BasePage } from './base-page';
import { BooksPage } from './books-page';

export class LoginPage extends BasePage {
  readonly path = '/login/';

  readonly heading: Locator;
  readonly usernameInput: Locator;
  readonly passwordInput: Locator;
  readonly signInButton: Locator;
  readonly formError: Locator;
  readonly usernameError: Locator;
  readonly passwordError: Locator;
  readonly createAccountLink: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.heading = page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Sign in' });
    this.usernameInput = page.getByLabel('Username');
    this.passwordInput = page.getByLabel('Password');
    this.signInButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' });
    this.formError = page.getByRole('alert');
    this.usernameError = page.locator('#username-error');
    this.passwordError = page.locator('#password-error');
    this.createAccountLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Create an account' });
  }

  async expectLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.heading).toBeVisible();
  }

  /** Fill the two fields and press the button. Does NOT check what happens next. */
  async submit(username: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.usernameInput.fill(username);
    await this.passwordInput.fill(password);
    await this.signInButton.click();
  }

  /** The happy path: sign in and hand back the page the user lands on. */
  async signInAs(user: TestUser): Promise<BooksPage> {
    await this.submit(user.username, user.password);
    const books = new BooksPage(this.page);
    await books.expectLoaded();
    return books;
  }

  async expectOnThisPage(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/\/login\//);
  }

  async expectFormError(message: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.formError).toHaveText(message);
  }
}
```

**Step 2 — `RegisterPage.registerAs`** returns the Sign-in page the site sends the user to:

*File: `e2e/pages/register-page.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';
import { BasePage } from './base-page';
import { LoginPage } from './login-page';

export class RegisterPage extends BasePage {
  readonly path = '/register/';

  readonly heading: Locator;
  readonly usernameInput: Locator;
  readonly passwordInput: Locator;
  readonly createButton: Locator;
  readonly usernameError: Locator;
  readonly passwordError: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.heading = page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Create an account' });
    this.usernameInput = page.getByLabel('Username');
    this.passwordInput = page.getByLabel('Password');
    this.createButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' });
    this.usernameError = page.locator('#username-error');
    this.passwordError = page.locator('#password-error');
  }

  async expectLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.heading).toBeVisible();
  }

  async fill(username: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.usernameInput.fill(username);
    await this.passwordInput.fill(password);
  }

  /** Create the account and hand back the Sign-in page the site sends the user to. */
  async registerAs(user: TestUser): Promise<LoginPage> {
    await this.fill(user.username, user.password);
    await this.createButton.click();
    const login = new LoginPage(this.page);
    await login.expectLoaded();
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/\/login\/$/);
    return login;
  }
}
```

**Step 3 — update the Sign-in tests.** Two places change. In the first test:

```ts
const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
await loginPage.signIn(user);
await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/);
await loginPage.header.expectSignedInAs(user.username);

// AFTER

const booksPage = await loginPage.signInAs(user);
await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/);
await booksPage.header.expectSignedInAs(user.username);
```

and in the wrong-password test, `registerAs` now hands over the page, so `const loginPage = new LoginPage(page)` disappears:

The complete updated file:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { LoginPage } from '../../pages/login-page';
import { RegisterPage } from '../../pages/register-page';
import { newUser } from '../../utils/ui-steps';

test.describe('Sign in', () => {
  test('a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page', async ({ page }) => {
    const user = newUser('anna');
    const registerPage = new RegisterPage(page);
    await registerPage.open(); // arrange: the account must exist
    const loginPage = await registerPage.registerAs(user);

    const booksPage = await loginPage.signInAs(user); // act: returns the page we land on

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/); // assert
    await booksPage.header.expectSignedInAs(user.username);
  });

  test('a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page', async ({ page }) => {
    const user = newUser();
    const registerPage = new RegisterPage(page);
    await registerPage.open();
    const loginPage = await registerPage.registerAs(user);

    await loginPage.submit(user.username, 'not-the-password');

    await loginPage.expectFormError('Invalid username or password.');
    await loginPage.expectOnThisPage();
  });

  test('an unknown user is rejected with the same message', async ({ page }) => {
    const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit('nobody_' + Date.now(), 'whatever-123');

    await loginPage.expectFormError('Invalid username or password.');
  });

  test('both fields are required', async ({ page }) => {
    const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.signInButton.click();

    await expect(loginPage.usernameError).toHaveText('Username is required.');
    await expect(loginPage.passwordError).toHaveText('Password is required.');
  });
});
```

**Step 4 — navigation tests.** Create `tests/framework/navigation.spec.ts`. To keep this lab self-contained it makes users with the old `newUser()` helper; Lab 5.5 replaces it.

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/navigation.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { BookFormPage, BooksPage, LoginPage, RegisterPage } from '../../pages';
import { newUser } from '../../utils/ui-steps';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';
import type { TestUser } from '../../utils/types';

/** Create an account and return the Sign-in page, using nothing but page objects. */
async function registerNewUser(page: Page): Promise<{ user: TestUser; loginPage: LoginPage }> {
  const user = newUser();
  const registerPage = new RegisterPage(page);
  await registerPage.open();
  const loginPage = await registerPage.registerAs(user);
  return { user, loginPage };
}

test.describe('Navigation', () => {
  test('every step returns the next page object, so a journey reads like a story', async ({ page }) => {
    const book = makeBook();

    const { user, loginPage } = await registerNewUser(page); // Create account -> Sign in
    const booksPage = await loginPage.signInAs(user); //        Sign in        -> Books
    const formPage = await booksPage.goToAddBook(); //          Books          -> Add book
    const backOnBooks = await formPage.save(book); //           Add book       -> Books

    await backOnBooks.expectBook(book.title);
  });

  test('an anonymous visitor is sent to Sign in, then returned to the page they asked for', async ({ page }) => {
    const { user, loginPage } = await registerNewUser(page);

    await page.goto('/books/new/'); // asking for a protected page while NOT signed in
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login\/\?next=%2Fbooks%2Fnew%2F$/);

    await loginPage.submit(user.username, user.password);

    await new BookFormPage(page).expectLoaded();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/new\/$/);
  });

  test('Cancel on the Add book form goes back to the list', async ({ page }) => {
    const { user, loginPage } = await registerNewUser(page);
    const booksPage = await loginPage.signInAs(user);

    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    await form.cancelLink.click();

    await booksPage.expectLoaded();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/);
  });

  test('the Book Library logo link goes to the Books page', async ({ page }) => {
    const { user, loginPage } = await registerNewUser(page);
    const booksPage = await loginPage.signInAs(user);
    await booksPage.goToAddBook();

    await booksPage.header.brandLink.click();

    await new BooksPage(page).expectLoaded();
  });
});
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `async signInAs(user): Promise<BooksPage>` | Fill, click, **wait** until the Books page is loaded, return its page object |
| `const books = new BooksPage(this.page)` | A new page object for the page the user is now on; it shares the same browser page |
| `async registerAs(user): Promise<LoginPage>` | After a successful registration the site shows the Sign-in page |
| `registerNewUser(page)` (helper in the spec) | A **local** helper: used only by this file, so it stays in the file. If a second file needs it, it moves to a fixture (Lab 5.4) |
| `await page.goto('/books/new/')` while signed out | The protected-page redirect is behaviour of the **application**, so the test checks the address directly |
| `/\/login\/\?next=%2Fbooks%2Fnew%2F$/` | The visitor is sent to Sign in, and the page they wanted is remembered in `next` (`%2F` is an encoded `/`) |
| `loginPage.submit(...)` then `new BookFormPage(page).expectLoaded()` | After this sign-in the user lands on **Add book**, not Books — so `signInAs` (which expects Books) would be the wrong method. A clear sign the two methods are different |
| `form.cancelLink.click()` | A one-off use of a public locator |
| `booksPage.header.brandLink.click()` | The logo is part of the **header component**, available on every page |

### Common mistakes

* **A navigation method that does not wait.** `return new BooksPage(page)` without `expectLoaded()` hands the test a page that may not exist yet.
* **Returning the wrong page** (copy-paste of `signInAs` for a button that leads elsewhere). The compiler cannot know what the application does — your tests check it.
* **Making the page object decide the story** ("after sign-in it also adds a book"). Keep methods single-purpose.
* **Using `signInAs` when the application sends the user somewhere else** (the `?next=` case). Use `submit` and check the real destination.

### Troubleshooting

Using the result of an action that does not return a page is caught by the compiler (a test that treats `submit()` — which returns nothing — as if it returned the Books page):

```text
tests/framework/zz-void.spec.ts(7,19): error TS2339: Property 'header' does not exist on type 'void'.
```

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `TS2339 Property 'header' does not exist on type 'void'` | The method you called returns nothing (`submit`, `fill`…) | Use the method that moves the user (`signInAs`, `registerAs`, `goToAddBook`…) and keep what it returns |
| `TS2305`/`TS2307` about `./books-page` or `./login-page` | A page object file was not created yet or is misnamed | Check the file names against the Files list |
| The test lands on the wrong page and times out | `signInAs` waits for the Books heading, but the application sent the user elsewhere (the `?next=` case) | Use `submit` and check the real destination |
| `Test timeout … waiting for getByRole('heading', { name: 'Books' })` | The sign-in failed (wrong credentials) so the Books page never came | Read the error on the Sign-in page in the screenshot/trace |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Add `signOut()` to the navigation story: sign in, then sign out, and check the *Sign in* page shows the confirmation message (the text is `You have been signed out.`).
2. Write a journey test with four chained pages that ends by **deleting** the book it added and checks it is gone.
3. In `RegisterPage`, add `goToSignIn()` that follows the *Sign in* link, if the page has one. Check the page first (DevTools). If it has no such link, write down what that tells you about the requirement.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

```ts

const loginAgain = await booksPage.signOut();
await loginAgain.notice.expectMessage('You have been signed out.');

// 2
const books = await (await (await login.signInAs(user)).goToAddBook()).save(book);
await books.deleteBook(book.title);
await books.expectNoBook(book.title);
```
3 — The Create-account page has no link back to Sign in, so a visitor who opens it by mistake has only the browser's Back button. That is a **usability finding** worth reporting; the page object should not invent a method for a link that does not exist.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 5.3)

1. What does a navigation method return, and why? *(The page object of the page the user lands on, so the compiler guides the next step.)*
2. Why do navigation methods wait for the next page? *(Otherwise the test races ahead of the browser.)*
3. When is a circular import between two page objects safe? *(When each uses the other only inside methods, not at load time such as `extends`.)*
4. Why did the `?next=` test use `submit` instead of `signInAs`? *(The user lands on Add book, not on Books.)*

## Lab 5.4 — Playwright fixtures and custom fixtures 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Explain what a **fixture** is and how it differs from `beforeEach`.
* Use Playwright's built-in fixtures (`page`, `context`, `browser`, `baseURL`).
* Write **custom fixtures** that hand a test a ready page object, a registered user, or a signed-in Books page.
* Write set-up **and tear-down** in one place, and an **automatic** fixture that watches every test.

### Concepts in simple language

You have used fixtures since Lab 3.1: `async ({ page }) => …` means *"Playwright, give me a fresh page"*. A **fixture** is a named thing a test can ask for in its parentheses. Playwright builds it only for the tests that ask, and cleans it up afterwards.

```ts
test('…', async ({ page, context, baseURL }) => { … })     // built-in fixtures
test('…', async ({ loginPage, registeredUser }) => { … })  // YOUR fixtures
```

**Why not just `beforeEach`?**

| | `beforeEach` | Fixture |
|---|---|---|
| Runs for | **every** test in its `describe`, wanted or not | only the tests that **ask** |
| Gives the test a value | through shared variables (awkward) | as a typed parameter |
| Clean-up | a separate `afterEach`, easy to forget | the lines after `use(...)`, next to the set-up |
| Reuse across files | copy-paste | `import { test } from '../../fixtures'` |
| Can depend on another | no | yes — a fixture can ask for other fixtures |

**The shape of a fixture:**

```ts
registeredUser: async ({ registerPage }, use) => {
  // 1) SET-UP: everything before use()
  const user = makeUser();
  await registerPage.open();
  await registerPage.registerAs(user);

  await use(user);          // 2) the TEST runs here, receiving `user`

  // 3) TEAR-DOWN: everything after use() runs when the test is over, even if it failed
},
```

**Three kinds you will write:**

| Kind | In this lab | Idea |
|---|---|---|
| **Object** fixtures | `loginPage`, `registerPage`, `bookFormPage` | Hand over a ready page object — no `new` in tests |
| **Data/state** fixtures | `registeredUser`, `booksPage` | Do the *arrange* part of Arrange–Act–Assert |
| **Automatic** fixtures | `failOnPageErrors` | `{ auto: true }`: run for **every** test, nobody asks |

Fixtures have a **scope**: the default is one per **test** (a fresh one each time — safe and isolated). A fixture can instead be shared by a whole **worker** (`{ scope: 'worker' }`) when it is slow and read-only; it is an advanced tool and we do not need it here.

### Why QA needs it

* A test starts with **one line of intent** (`async ({ booksPage }) => …`) instead of ten lines of preparation.
* Set-up and clean-up live together, so a change is made once.
* Cross-cutting rules ("no JavaScript error may go unnoticed") apply to **all** tests without anyone remembering.

### Prerequisites

Labs 5.1–5.3.

### Files

```
fixtures/index.ts                       NEW  the custom `test`
tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts         CHANGED  uses fixtures (+ a sign-out test)
tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts      CHANGED  uses fixtures (+ the "another user" test)
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the fixtures file.** Create `fixtures/index.ts`. It extends Playwright's `test` and **exports it again**; tests import `test` from here instead of from `@playwright/test`. (It borrows `newUser` from the old helper file for one more lab.)

*File: `e2e/fixtures/index.ts`*

```ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { BookFormPage, BooksPage, LoginPage, RegisterPage } from '../pages';
import { newUser } from '../utils/ui-steps';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';

/** The names a test can ask for, and the type of each. */
interface Fixtures {
  /** Page objects that are ready to use (the browser is on a blank page). */
  loginPage: LoginPage;
  registerPage: RegisterPage;
  bookFormPage: BookFormPage;
  /** A new user whose account exists on the server but who is NOT signed in. */
  registeredUser: TestUser;
  /** The Books page of a freshly registered, signed-in user. The usual starting point. */
  booksPage: BooksPage;
  /** AUTOMATIC: fails the test when the page throws an unhandled JavaScript error. */
  failOnPageErrors: void;
}

export const test = base.extend<Fixtures>({
  loginPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new LoginPage(page));
  },

  registerPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new RegisterPage(page));
  },

  bookFormPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new BookFormPage(page));
  },

  // A fixture can use other fixtures: this one needs registerPage.
  registeredUser: async ({ registerPage }, use) => {
    const user = newUser();
    await test.step('arrange: register a new user', async () => {
      await registerPage.open();
      await registerPage.registerAs(user);
    });
    await use(user); // <- the test runs here
    // Code after `use` is the TEARDOWN. (The application has no "delete user" button;
    // Phase 6 shows how an API call can clean up.)
  },

  booksPage: async ({ page, loginPage, registeredUser }, use) => {
    await test.step('arrange: sign in', async () => {
      await loginPage.open();
      await loginPage.signInAs(registeredUser);
    });
    await use(new BooksPage(page));
  },

  failOnPageErrors: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      const errors: string[] = [];
      page.on('pageerror', (error) => errors.push(error.message));
      await use();
      expect(errors, 'the page threw JavaScript errors').toEqual([]);
    },
    { auto: true }, // runs for EVERY test that imports this `test`, even when not asked for
  ],
});

export { expect };
```

**Step 2 — use them.** Replace `tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`. Compare the first test with the Lab 5.3 version: the whole *arrange* part has disappeared into the `registeredUser` fixture. (Messages are still plain strings; Lab 5.5 moves them.)

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';
import { newUser } from '../../utils/ui-steps';

test.describe('Sign in', () => {
  test('a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page', async ({ page, loginPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    const books = await loginPage.signInAs(registeredUser);

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/);
    await books.header.expectSignedInAs(registeredUser.username);
  });

  test('a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page', async ({ loginPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit(registeredUser.username, 'not-the-password');

    await loginPage.expectFormError('Invalid username or password.');
    await loginPage.expectOnThisPage();
  });

  test('an unknown user is rejected with the same message', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    const stranger = newUser('nobody');
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit(stranger.username, stranger.password);

    await loginPage.expectFormError('Invalid username or password.');
  });

  test('both fields are required', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.signInButton.click();

    await expect(loginPage.usernameError).toHaveText('Username is required.');
    await expect(loginPage.passwordError).toHaveText('Password is required.');
  });

  test('signing out returns to Sign in with a confirmation', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const loginPage = await booksPage.signOut();

    await loginPage.notice.expectMessage('You have been signed out.');
  });
});
```

**Step 3 — the Books tests.** Replace `tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts`. It asks for `booksPage` — a signed-in user already looking at the Books page — and gets a sixth test that uses a **second browser context**:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test } from '../../fixtures';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';
import { newUser } from '../../utils/ui-steps';
import { RegisterPage } from '../../pages';

test.describe('Books: add, edit, delete', () => {
  test('an added book appears in the list with its details', async ({ booksPage, registeredUser }) => {
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: 1984 });

    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    const books = await form.save(book);

    await books.notice.expectMessage('Book added.');
    await books.expectRow(book.title, { author: book.author, year: '1984', owner: registeredUser.username });
  });

  test('the year is optional: a book without one shows a dash', async ({ booksPage, registeredUser }) => {
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: null });

    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    const books = await form.save(book);

    await books.expectRow(book.title, { author: book.author, year: '—', owner: registeredUser.username });
  });

  test('editing a book changes its title', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    const form = await books.goToEditBook(book.title);
    const newTitle = `${book.title} (2nd ed.)`;
    const updated = await form.save({ ...book, title: newTitle });

    await updated.notice.expectMessage('Book updated.');
    await updated.expectBook(newTitle);
    await updated.expectNoBook(book.title);
  });

  test('deleting a book removes it after the user confirms', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    await books.deleteBook(book.title);

    await books.notice.expectMessage('Book deleted.');
    await books.expectNoBook(book.title);
  });

  test('cancelling the delete dialog keeps the book', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    await books.startDeleting(book.title);
    await books.confirmDialog.cancel();

    await books.expectBook(book.title);
  });

  test('another user sees the book but has no Edit or Delete controls', async ({ booksPage, browser }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    // A SECOND browser context = a second person. Page objects work on any page you give them.
    const context = await browser.newContext();
    try {
      const stranger = newUser('visitor');
      const strangerPage = await context.newPage();
      const login = await (async () => {
        const register = new RegisterPage(strangerPage);
        await register.open();
        return register.registerAs(stranger);
      })();
      const theirBooks = await login.signInAs(stranger);

      await theirBooks.search(book.title);
      await theirBooks.expectBook(book.title);
      await theirBooks.expectOwnerControls(book.title, false);
    } finally {
      await context.close();
    }
  });
});
```

```powershell
npx playwright test tests/framework --project=chromium
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `interface Fixtures { loginPage: LoginPage; … }` | Tells TypeScript the **name** and **type** of every custom fixture. Without it `{ loginPage }` would be a compile error |
| `base.extend<Fixtures>({ … })` | Creates a new `test` that has all the old fixtures plus yours |
| `loginPage: async ({ page }, use) => { await use(new LoginPage(page)); }` | An **object fixture**: it builds the page object and hands it over. Needs the built-in `page` fixture |
| `registeredUser: async ({ registerPage }, use)` | A fixture that depends on another fixture. Playwright builds `registerPage` first |
| `test.step('arrange: …', …)` | Names a block. It appears in the HTML report and in the trace, so a failure says "arrange: sign in" instead of pointing at fixture code |
| `await use(user)` | The test runs now. Code after this line is **tear-down** |
| `booksPage: async ({ page, loginPage, registeredUser }, use)` | Needs three fixtures. The test that asks for `booksPage` **and** `registeredUser` gets the **same** user object — fixtures are cached per test |
| `failOnPageErrors: [ async … , { auto: true } ]` | An **automatic** fixture: the array form adds options. It collects `pageerror` events and, after the test, fails if there were any |
| `export { expect }` | Re-exports `expect`, so a test needs only one import line |
| `browser` fixture in the last test | Built-in. `browser.newContext()` makes a second, separate person (own cookies) |
| `try { … } finally { await context.close(); }` | A context you create yourself is **your** job to close, even when an assertion throws |
| `makeUser('visitor')` / `newUser('visitor')` | A new account for the second person |

```ts
  await register(page, user);                          …
  await page.getByLabel('Username').fill(…);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(…);

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading',…)).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole('link', {name:'Add book'}).click();
  …
```

### See the automatic fixture work

Create a temporary file `tests/framework/zz-page-error.spec.ts`. The test itself finds nothing wrong, but the page **throws a JavaScript error** a moment after loading:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/zz-page-error.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';

test('a page that throws a JavaScript error', async ({ page, loginPage }) => {
  await loginPage.open();
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    setTimeout(() => {
      throw new Error('boom from the page');
    }, 0);
  });
  await page.evaluate(() => 1); // one more round trip, so the error has arrived
  await expect(loginPage.heading).toBeVisible(); // the test itself is happy...
});
```

Run it:

```powershell
npx playwright test tests/framework/zz-page-error.spec.ts --project=chromium
```

```text
  1) [chromium] › tests/framework/zz-page-error.spec.ts:3:5 › a page that throws a JavaScript error 

    Error: the page threw JavaScript errors

    expect(received).toEqual(expected) // deep equality

    - Expected  - 1
    + Received  + 3

    - Array []
    + Array [
    +   "boom from the page",
    + ]

       at ../fixtures/index.ts:58
```

The test fails **in the fixture's tear-down**, with a message that names the cause. Without the automatic fixture this test would have passed and the broken page would have gone unnoticed. **Delete the temporary file** before you continue.

### Common mistakes

* **Importing `test` from `@playwright/test` in a spec that needs your fixtures.** Then `booksPage` is "not a known fixture". Import from `'../../fixtures'`.
* **Forgetting `await use(...)`** (or calling it twice). A fixture calls `use` exactly once.
* **Putting assertions about the product into a fixture.** A fixture *arranges*; the test *asserts*. (Checking that set-up worked — "the Books heading appears" — is fine and is done by `expectLoaded()`.)
* **A fixture that does too much.** `booksPage` signs in and nothing else. A fixture "that also creates ten books" belongs in a second fixture with its own name.
* **Sharing mutable state between tests through a worker-scoped fixture** and breaking isolation (Lab 4.9).
* **Hiding which user the test uses.** If the test needs the user's name, it asks for `registeredUser` as well; the same user comes back.

### Troubleshooting

The most common mistake — a spec that imports the plain `test` but asks for a custom fixture. The compiler says:

```text
tests/framework/zz-wrong-import.spec.ts(3,71): error TS2339: Property 'booksPage' does not exist on type 'PlaywrightTestArgs & PlaywrightTestOptions & PlaywrightWorkerArgs & PlaywrightWorkerOptions'.
```

and Playwright, if you run it anyway:

```text
Test has unknown parameter "booksPage".

   at framework/zz-wrong-import.spec.ts:3
```

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Test has unknown parameter "booksPage"` / `TS2339 Property 'booksPage' does not exist` | The spec imports `test` from `@playwright/test` | `import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures'` |
| `TS2339` for a fixture you did write | The name is missing from `interface Fixtures` | Add it, with its type |
| The page is blank / not signed in in a fixture-based test | The fixture opened the page but you forgot `await` somewhere | Every page-object call needs `await` |
| A test is slower than expected | An automatic fixture does heavy work | Automatic fixtures must be cheap; make heavy ones normal (on request) |

### Knowledge check (Lab 5.4)

1. What does `await use(value)` do in a fixture? *(Hands the value to the test and waits for it to finish; code after it is tear-down.)*
2. Give two advantages of fixtures over `beforeEach`. *(Only run when asked; typed values; set-up and tear-down together; reusable across files; composable.)*
3. What is an automatic fixture? *(`{ auto: true }`: it runs for every test, even when not requested.)*
4. Why do `booksPage` and `registeredUser` refer to the same user in one test? *(Fixtures are created once per test and cached.)*
5. Who closes a browser context you made with `browser.newContext()`? *(You — use `try/finally`.)*

## Lab 5.5 — Test data management 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Separate **three kinds of data**: facts (messages), builders (unique records) and tables (JSON).
* Replace "magic strings" and one-off data with named, typed, shared definitions.
* Keep every test independent in a **shared** library.
* Add new tests quickly because the data layer already exists.

### Concepts in simple language

Your tests contain three kinds of data. Each has its own home:

| Kind | Example | Home | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Facts about the product** | The text `Invalid username or password.` | `data/messages.ts` | A constant object, `as const` |
| **Records the test creates** | A user, a book | `data/users.ts`, `utils/test-data.ts`, `data/books.ts` | **Builder functions** that make a **unique** record every call |
| **Tables of cases** | The nine year values, the five form cases | `data/*.json` | One file; the test loops over it (Lab 4.7) |

**Why messages deserve a file.** If product says "Title is required." becomes "Please enter a title.", you want to edit **one** line, not 12 tests. The test still *states* the requirement (`MESSAGES.book.titleRequired`) — it just reads it from the one list.

**Why builders return unique data.** The library is shared by every test and every user (Lab 3.8). `makeBook()` puts a random token in the title and the author, so a test can search for exactly its own books. `smallLibrary()` puts the token **first** in every title, so one search finds the whole set.

**Rules for test data**

1. **Never** depend on data another test created.
2. Make data **unique** per run; never hard-code a username.
3. Passwords come from the environment (Lab 5.6), never from the code.
4. A builder returns a **plain object** typed with an `interface`, so the editor completes the fields.
5. Keep **big** data (a CSV, long JSON) in files; keep **small** facts in TypeScript.

### Why QA needs it

Data is where flaky tests are born (collisions, leftovers) and where copy-paste hides (the same title in ten files). A tidy data layer makes tests parallel-safe and product text changes cheap.

### Prerequisites

Lab 5.4.
