tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts      CHANGED  MESSAGES
tests/framework/navigation.spec.ts      CHANGED  makeUser, no tags yet
tests/framework/register.spec.ts        NEW  Create-account tests
tests/framework/books-list.spec.ts      NEW  search and sort
tests/framework/book-form-validation.spec.ts   NEW  data-driven validation
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the messages.** Create `data/messages.ts`:

*File: `e2e/data/messages.ts`*

```ts
/**
 * Every piece of text the application shows and the tests check, in ONE place.
 * If the product team rewords a message, you change it here once - not in 30 tests.
 */
export const MESSAGES = {
  signIn: {
    invalidCredentials: 'Invalid username or password.',
    usernameRequired: 'Username is required.',
    passwordRequired: 'Password is required.',
    signedOut: 'You have been signed out.',
  },
  register: {
    created: 'Account created. Please sign in.',
    duplicateUsername: 'A user with that username already exists.',
  },
  book: {
    added: 'Book added.',
    updated: 'Book updated.',
    deleted: 'Book deleted.',
    titleRequired: 'Title is required.',
    authorRequired: 'Author is required.',
    yearNotWhole: 'Year must be a whole number.',
    yearOutOfRange: 'Year must be between 1000 and 2100.',
  },
} as const;
```

**Step 2 — the user builder** and **Step 3 — the book builder.** Create `data/users.ts`:

*File: `e2e/data/users.ts`*

```ts
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';
import { env } from '../utils/env';
import { uniqueUsername } from '../utils/test-data';

/** A user that does not exist yet. The name is unique, the password comes from the environment. */
export function makeUser(prefix = 'qa'): TestUser {
  return { username: uniqueUsername(prefix), password: env.testUserPassword };
}
```

and `data/books.ts`:

*File: `e2e/data/books.ts`*

```ts
import type { BookData } from '../utils/types';
import { uid } from '../utils/test-data';

/**
 * Three named books for tests that need "a small library".
 * The token comes FIRST in every title, so a search for the token finds exactly these three,
 * even though the library is shared with every other test and user.
 */
export function smallLibrary(token: string = uid()): { token: string; books: BookData[] } {
  return {
    token,
    books: [
      { title: `${token} Emma`, author: 'Jane Austen', published_year: 1815 },
      { title: `${token} Persuasion`, author: 'Jane Austen', published_year: 1817 },
      { title: `${token} Dune`, author: 'Frank Herbert', published_year: 1965 },
    ],
  };
}
```

**Step 4 — point the fixtures at the new builder.** In `fixtures/index.ts` change one import and one call (the file is shown whole so you can compare):

```ts
// BEFORE
import { newUser } from '../utils/ui-steps';        …   const user = newUser();
// AFTER
import { makeUser } from '../data/users';           …   const user = makeUser();
```

*File: `e2e/fixtures/index.ts`*

```ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { BookFormPage, BooksPage, LoginPage, RegisterPage } from '../pages';
import { makeUser } from '../data/users';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';

/** The names a test can ask for, and the type of each. */
interface Fixtures {
  /** Page objects that are ready to use (the browser is on a blank page). */
  loginPage: LoginPage;
  registerPage: RegisterPage;
  bookFormPage: BookFormPage;
  /** A new user whose account exists on the server but who is NOT signed in. */
  registeredUser: TestUser;
  /** The Books page of a freshly registered, signed-in user. The usual starting point. */
  booksPage: BooksPage;
  /** AUTOMATIC: fails the test when the page throws an unhandled JavaScript error. */
  failOnPageErrors: void;
}

export const test = base.extend<Fixtures>({
  loginPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new LoginPage(page));
  },

  registerPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new RegisterPage(page));
  },

  bookFormPage: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(new BookFormPage(page));
  },

  // A fixture can use other fixtures: this one needs registerPage.
  registeredUser: async ({ registerPage }, use) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    await test.step('arrange: register a new user', async () => {
      await registerPage.open();
      await registerPage.registerAs(user);
    });
    await use(user); // <- the test runs here
    // Code after `use` is the TEARDOWN. (The application has no "delete user" button;
    // Phase 6 shows how an API call can clean up.)
  },

  booksPage: async ({ page, loginPage, registeredUser }, use) => {
    await test.step('arrange: sign in', async () => {
      await loginPage.open();
      await loginPage.signInAs(registeredUser);
    });
    await use(new BooksPage(page));
  },

  failOnPageErrors: [
    async ({ page }, use) => {
      const errors: string[] = [];
      page.on('pageerror', (error) => errors.push(error.message));
      await use();
      expect(errors, 'the page threw JavaScript errors').toEqual([]);
    },
    { auto: true }, // runs for EVERY test that imports this `test`, even when not asked for
  ],
});

export { expect };
```

**Step 5 — use `MESSAGES` in the two spec files you already have.** Every literal such as `'Book added.'` becomes `MESSAGES.book.added`; add the import `import { MESSAGES } from '../../data/messages';` and, in `sign-in.spec.ts`, `makeUser` from `'../../data/users'`. In `navigation.spec.ts` change only the import: `import { makeUser } from '../../data/users';` and the call `newUser()` → `makeUser()`. The three updated files:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';
import { MESSAGES } from '../../data/messages';
import { makeUser } from '../../data/users';

test.describe('Sign in', () => {
  test('a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page', async ({ page, loginPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    const books = await loginPage.signInAs(registeredUser);

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/);
    await books.header.expectSignedInAs(registeredUser.username);
  });

  test('a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page', async ({ loginPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit(registeredUser.username, 'not-the-password');

    await loginPage.expectFormError(MESSAGES.signIn.invalidCredentials);
    await loginPage.expectOnThisPage();
  });

  test('an unknown user is rejected with the same message', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    const stranger = makeUser('nobody');
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit(stranger.username, stranger.password);

    await loginPage.expectFormError(MESSAGES.signIn.invalidCredentials);
  });

  test('both fields are required', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.signInButton.click();

    await expect(loginPage.usernameError).toHaveText(MESSAGES.signIn.usernameRequired);
    await expect(loginPage.passwordError).toHaveText(MESSAGES.signIn.passwordRequired);
  });

  test('signing out returns to Sign in with a confirmation', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const loginPage = await booksPage.signOut();

    await loginPage.notice.expectMessage(MESSAGES.signIn.signedOut);
  });
});
```

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/books-crud.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test } from '../../fixtures';
import { MESSAGES } from '../../data/messages';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';
import { makeUser } from '../../data/users';
import { RegisterPage } from '../../pages';

test.describe('Books: add, edit, delete', () => {
  test('an added book appears in the list with its details', async ({ booksPage, registeredUser }) => {
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: 1984 });

    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    const books = await form.save(book);

    await books.notice.expectMessage(MESSAGES.book.added);
    await books.expectRow(book.title, { author: book.author, year: '1984', owner: registeredUser.username });
  });

  test('the year is optional: a book without one shows a dash', async ({ booksPage, registeredUser }) => {
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: null });

    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    const books = await form.save(book);

    await books.expectRow(book.title, { author: book.author, year: '—', owner: registeredUser.username });
  });

  test('editing a book changes its title', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    const form = await books.goToEditBook(book.title);
    const newTitle = `${book.title} (2nd ed.)`;
    const updated = await form.save({ ...book, title: newTitle });

    await updated.notice.expectMessage(MESSAGES.book.updated);
    await updated.expectBook(newTitle);
    await updated.expectNoBook(book.title);
  });

  test('deleting a book removes it after the user confirms', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    await books.deleteBook(book.title);

    await books.notice.expectMessage(MESSAGES.book.deleted);
    await books.expectNoBook(book.title);
  });

  test('cancelling the delete dialog keeps the book', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const books = await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    await books.startDeleting(book.title);
    await books.confirmDialog.cancel();

    await books.expectBook(book.title);
  });

  test('another user sees the book but has no Edit or Delete controls', async ({ booksPage, browser }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    await (await booksPage.goToAddBook()).save(book);

    // A SECOND browser context = a second person. Page objects work on any page you give them.
    const context = await browser.newContext();
    try {
      const stranger = makeUser('visitor');
      const strangerPage = await context.newPage();
      const login = await (async () => {
        const register = new RegisterPage(strangerPage);
        await register.open();
        return register.registerAs(stranger);
      })();
      const theirBooks = await login.signInAs(stranger);

      await theirBooks.search(book.title);
      await theirBooks.expectBook(book.title);
      await theirBooks.expectOwnerControls(book.title, false);
    } finally {
      await context.close();
    }
  });
});
```

(`navigation.spec.ts` is unchanged apart from the import, so it is not repeated.)

**Step 6 — three new spec files, written the framework way.** Notice how short they are now that pages, fixtures and data exist.

`tests/framework/register.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/register.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';
import { MESSAGES } from '../../data/messages';
import { makeUser } from '../../data/users';

test.describe('Create account', () => {
  test('the button stays disabled until both fields are filled', async ({ registerPage }) => {
    await registerPage.open();
    await expect(registerPage.createButton).toBeDisabled();

    await registerPage.usernameInput.fill('someone');
    await expect(registerPage.createButton).toBeDisabled(); // still waiting for the password

    await registerPage.passwordInput.fill('S3cure-Lab-Passw0rd!');
    await expect(registerPage.createButton).toBeEnabled();
  });

  test('registering sends the new user to Sign in with a confirmation', async ({ registerPage }) => {
    await registerPage.open();
    const loginPage = await registerPage.registerAs(makeUser());

    await loginPage.notice.expectMessage(MESSAGES.register.created);
  });

  test('a username that is already taken is refused', async ({ registerPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await registerPage.open();
    await registerPage.fill(registeredUser.username, registeredUser.password);
    await registerPage.createButton.click();

    await expect(registerPage.usernameError).toHaveText(MESSAGES.register.duplicateUsername);
  });
});

`tests/framework/books-list.spec.ts` (search and sort, with a small library of known books):

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/books-list.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';
import { smallLibrary } from '../../data/books';
import { BooksPage } from '../../pages';

test.describe('Books list: search and sort', () => {
  /** Arrange: put three known books into the shared library and hand back the Books page. */
  async function withSmallLibrary(booksPage: BooksPage) {
    const { token, books } = smallLibrary();
    for (const book of books) {
      const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
      await form.save(book);
    }
    return { token, titles: books.map((b) => b.title) };
  }

  test('searching for a title narrows the list', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const { token, titles } = await withSmallLibrary(booksPage);

    await booksPage.search(token);
    await expect(booksPage.rows).toHaveCount(3);
    await expect(booksPage.countText).toHaveText('3 books');

    await booksPage.search(titles[2]); // the Dune title
    await expect(booksPage.rows).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(booksPage.countText).toHaveText('1 book');
  });

  test('search also matches the author', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const { token } = await withSmallLibrary(booksPage);

    await booksPage.search('Frank Herbert');
    await expect(booksPage.rowFor(`${token} Dune`)).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(booksPage.rowFor(`${token} Emma`)).toHaveCount(0);
  });

  test('a search with no match says so', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const { token } = await withSmallLibrary(booksPage);

    await booksPage.search(`nothing-${token}`);

    await expect(booksPage.rows).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(booksPage.emptyMessage).toContainText('No books match');
  });

  test('titles can be sorted A to Z and Z to A', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const { token, titles } = await withSmallLibrary(booksPage);
    const [emma, persuasion, dune] = titles;
    await booksPage.search(token); // keep only OUR books: the library is shared

    await booksPage.sortBy('title');
    await booksPage.expectTitlesInOrder([dune, emma, persuasion]);

    await booksPage.sortBy('-title');
    await booksPage.expectTitlesInOrder([persuasion, emma, dune]);
  });

  test('books can be sorted by year, oldest first', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const { token, titles } = await withSmallLibrary(booksPage);
    const [emma, persuasion, dune] = titles; // 1815, 1817, 1965
    await booksPage.search(token);

    await booksPage.sortBy('published_year');
    await booksPage.expectTitlesInOrder([emma, persuasion, dune]);
  });
});
```

`tests/framework/book-form-validation.spec.ts` (the two JSON tables of Lab 4.7, now through page objects):

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/book-form-validation.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';
import yearCases from '../../data/year-cases.json';
import formCases from '../../data/book-form-cases.json';
import { BooksPage, type FormErrors } from '../../pages';
import { MESSAGES } from '../../data/messages';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';

/** The JSON lists messages; the form shows each one in its own place. Decide which by the first word. */
function toFormErrors(messages: string[]): FormErrors {
  const errors: FormErrors = {};
  for (const message of messages) {
    if (message.startsWith('Title')) errors.title = message;
    else if (message.startsWith('Author')) errors.author = message;
    else errors.year = message;
  }
  return errors;
}

test.describe('Add book form: validation', () => {
  for (const c of yearCases) {
    test(`year "${c.input}" - ${c.name}`, async ({ page, booksPage }) => {
      const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
      const book = makeBook();
      await form.fill({ title: book.title, author: book.author, published_year: c.input });
      await form.submit();

      if (c.expected === null) {
        await new BooksPage(page).expectLoaded(); // saved: we are back on the list
      } else {
        await form.expectErrors({ year: c.expected });
        await form.expectStillOnForm();
      }
    });
  }

  for (const c of formCases) {
    test(`whole form: ${c.name}`, async ({ page, booksPage }) => {
      const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
      await form.fill({ title: c.form.title, author: c.form.author, published_year: c.form.year });
      await form.submit();

      if (c.expectedErrors.length === 0) {
        await new BooksPage(page).expectLoaded();
      } else {
        await form.expectErrors(toFormErrors(c.expectedErrors));
        await form.expectStillOnForm();
      }
    });
  }

  test('an empty form uses the shared message texts', async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const form = await booksPage.goToAddBook();
    await form.submit();
    await form.expectErrors({ title: MESSAGES.book.titleRequired, author: MESSAGES.book.authorRequired });
    await expect(form.saveButton).toBeEnabled();
  });
});
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `export const MESSAGES = { … } as const` | `as const` freezes the shape: every value is the exact literal type, and a typo like `MESSAGES.book.addd` is a compile error |
| `signIn: { invalidCredentials: … }` | Grouped by area, so the editor's auto-complete lists the right options |
| `makeUser(prefix = 'qa')` | A user with a **unique** name and the environment's password |
| `smallLibrary(token = uid())` | Returns `{ token, books }`; a **default parameter** makes the token optional |
| `{ token, books: [ … ] }` — token first in each title | Searching the token finds exactly these three books in a shared library |
| `import yearCases from '../../data/year-cases.json'` | TypeScript reads the JSON and **infers its type** (`resolveJsonModule`, Lab 2.8) |
| `for (const c of yearCases) { test(…) }` | One test **per row**, each with its own name |
| `toFormErrors(messages)` | Turns the JSON's flat list of messages into the `{ title?, author?, year? }` the form page expects, by the first word of each message |
| `await form.expectErrors(toFormErrors(c.expectedErrors))` | One call checks all three message areas, including "no message" |
| `withSmallLibrary(booksPage)` (in `books-list.spec.ts`) | A **local** helper for the *arrange* part; it adds three books and returns their token and titles |
| `await booksPage.search(token)` before `sortBy` | Narrow to our own books first, then sort: the order of the whole library depends on everybody |
| `expectTitlesInOrder([dune, emma, persuasion])` | Titles share the token, so the sort order is decided by the word after it |

### Where does each piece of data live now?

| Question | File |
|---|---|
| What does the app say after a wrong password? | `data/messages.ts` |
| Who is the test user and what is the password? | `data/users.ts` + `utils/env.ts` |
| What books does a search test need? | `data/books.ts` |
| Which year values are valid? | `data/year-cases.json` + `utils/book-rules.ts` |

### Common mistakes

* **Messages hard-coded in the page object** — then the requirement is invisible in the test. Keep them in `data/messages.ts` and let the **test** choose which one to expect.
* **A hard-coded username** (`'testuser1'`). The second run collides with the first.
* **Data builders that share one object** (a module-level `const book = {…}` reused by every test). Tests then change each other's data. Always return a new object from a function.
* **Over-engineering:** a builder with 20 options for a form with 3 fields. Add options when a second test needs them.
* **JSON for everything.** Behaviour and logic go in code; JSON holds simple tables.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `TS2307 Cannot find module '../../data/year-cases.json'` | Wrong relative path, or `resolveJsonModule` is off | Count the `../`; check `tsconfig.json` |
| `Property 'addd' does not exist on type …` (MESSAGES) | A typo — caught for free | Fix the name |
| A sort test sees books from other users | The test did not search for its token first | `await booksPage.search(token)` |
| `"year "   " - spaces only"` shows odd spacing in the test name | The data contains spaces | Expected — it is the input value in quotes |

1. Add `bookWithoutYear()` to `data/books.ts` (a unique book with `published_year: null`). Use it in the "year is optional" test. Is it worth it for one test?
2. Add a message to `data/messages.ts` that the **Books** page shows when the list is empty and no search is active (`No books yet. Add the first one!`) and think about **why** this cannot be tested reliably on the shared library. What would you need?
3. Search the project for the literal `'Invalid username or password.'` with `Select-String`. How many places still contain it? Are those places acceptable?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

1. ```ts
   export function bookWithoutYear(): BookData { return makeBook({ published_year: null }); }
   ```
   For a single test it is just a rename, so it is optional. It pays off when a second test needs it, and it gives the idea a **name** (the test reads better).
2. The shared library almost always contains other people's books, so "no books at all" is not a state a test can create. You need a clean database (a dedicated test environment) or a mocked response (Lab 4.8).
3. Phase 3/4 files still contain it (`02-login.spec.ts`, mocking tests). They are the *old* tests; the new framework tests use `MESSAGES`. In a real project you would move or delete the old copies (Lab 5.9).
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 5.5)

1. Name the three kinds of data and their homes. *(Facts → `messages.ts`; unique records → builders; tables → JSON.)*
2. Why does `smallLibrary` put the token first in every title? *(So one search for the token finds exactly those books.)*
3. What does `as const` give you? *(Exact literal types; typos become compile errors.)*
4. Why should a test read the expected message from `MESSAGES` instead of the page object? *(The requirement stays visible in the test; one place changes when the product text changes.)*
5. Why return a new object from a builder every time? *(Shared mutable data makes tests affect each other.)*

## Lab 5.6 — Multiple environments, base URL, environment variables, configuration 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Run the same tests against **different environments** (local, CI, staging) without editing code.
* Explain the **order of precedence**: environment variable, `.env` file, built-in table.
* Keep secrets out of Git with `.env` and `.env.example`.
* Read configuration in **one** module.

### Concepts in simple language

A test suite is useful in more than one place: on your laptop, on the build server, against a shared "staging" system before a release. Only a few things change between those places — mainly the **address** of the application (the *base URL*) and sometimes a password. The tests themselves must **not** change.

| Idea | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Environment** | A named place where the application runs | `local`, `ci`, `staging` |
| **Base URL** | The part of the address every test shares. Playwright joins it to `page.goto('/login/')` | `http://localhost:8000` |
| **Environment variable** | A setting given to a program from outside, by name | `TEST_ENV=ci`, `BASE_URL=…` |
| **`.env` file** | A text file of `NAME=value` lines for **your** machine; never committed | `TEST_ENV=local` |
| **Configuration module** | The single code file that reads settings | `utils/env.ts` |
| **Secret** | A value that must not appear in Git or logs | a password, a token |

**Order of precedence** — which value wins when the same setting is given in several places (strongest first):

```
1. a real environment variable    BASE_URL=... set in the shell or by the CI server
2. a line in the .env file        your private, per-machine settings
3. the table in config/environments.ts, chosen by TEST_ENV   (default: local)
```

This lets a CI server override anything with no file edits, lets you keep personal settings in `.env`, and gives everyone sensible defaults.

### Why QA needs it

"It works on my machine" is the most expensive sentence in testing. Environment configuration is how the same suite runs in many places and how you avoid the two classic accidents: tests that secretly run against the wrong system, and passwords pushed to a public repository.

### Prerequisites

Lab 5.5.

### Files

```
config/environments.ts                 NEW  the table of environments
utils/env.ts                           CHANGED  reads .env, TEST_ENV and BASE_URL
.env.example                           NEW  a template (committed); your real `.env` is not
tests/framework/environment.spec.ts    NEW  tests for the configuration itself
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the table of environments.** Create `config/environments.ts`:

*File: `e2e/config/environments.ts`*

```ts
/** One entry per place the tests can run against. Add a line here to add an environment. */
export interface Environment {
  /** Where the application is running. */
  baseUrl: string;
  /** Shown in logs, so a person can see which one was used. */
  description: string;
}

export const environments: Record<string, Environment> = {
  local: { baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8000', description: 'the app on my own computer' },
  ci: { baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8000', description: 'the app started by the build server' },
  staging: { baseUrl: 'https://staging.booklibrary.example', description: 'the shared test server' },
};

export const DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT = 'local';
```

> **Added in Phase 7.** Change the `ci` address to `http://localhost:8000`. The application sets `Secure` cookies, and Playwright's API client sends them back over plain `http://` only to `localhost`, not to `127.0.0.1`. With the address above, every API call on a build server fails with *CSRF cookie not set*. Lab 7.10 (Case 1) reproduces and explains it.

**Step 2 — the one module that reads settings.** Replace `utils/env.ts`:

*File: `e2e/utils/env.ts`*

```ts
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT, environments } from '../config/environments';

/**
 * ONE place that reads configuration. Everything else imports `env`.
 *
 * Order of precedence (strongest first):
 *   1. a real environment variable   (BASE_URL=... set in the shell or by the CI server)
 *   2. a line in the `.env` file      (your private settings; never committed)
 *   3. the table in config/environments.ts, chosen by TEST_ENV   (default: local)
 */
if (existsSync('.env')) process.loadEnvFile('.env'); // Node 20.12+. Never overwrites variables that are already set.

const name = process.env.TEST_ENV ?? DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT;
const chosen = environments[name];
if (!chosen) {
  throw new Error(`Unknown TEST_ENV "${name}". Choose one of: ${Object.keys(environments).join(', ')}.`);
}

export const env = {
  /** The name of the environment in use: local, ci, staging... */
  name,
  description: chosen.description,

  /** BASE_URL wins over the table, so one-off runs need no code change. */
  baseUrl: (process.env.BASE_URL ?? chosen.baseUrl).replace(/\/+$/, ''),

  // A password for the test users. Use the environment variable when it is set;
  // otherwise make a strong random one for this run. Nothing secret lives in the code.
  testUserPassword: process.env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD || `Pw-${randomBytes(9).toString('hex')}-Aa1!`,
};
```

**Step 3 — a template for private settings.** Create `.env.example` (committed to Git). Each student copies it to `.env`, which `.gitignore` already hides (since Lab 3.1):

*File: `e2e/.env.example`*

```text
TEST_ENV=local
# BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000
# TEST_USER_PASSWORD=choose-a-strong-one
```

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

**Step 4 — tests for the configuration.** Create `tests/framework/environment.spec.ts`. Two of its tests start a **separate Node process** with different variables, because `env.ts` reads them only once, when it is first loaded:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/environment.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { env } from '../../utils/env';
import { environments } from '../../config/environments';

test.describe('Configuration', () => {
  test('the browser is pointed at the selected environment', async ({ baseURL }) => {
    expect(Object.keys(environments)).toContain(env.name);
    expect(baseURL).toBe(env.baseUrl);
  });

  test('an unknown TEST_ENV is refused with a helpful message', () => {
    const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--import', 'tsx', '-e', "import('./utils/env')"], {
      env: { ...process.env, TEST_ENV: 'nowhere' },
      encoding: 'utf8',
    });
    expect(result.status).not.toBe(0);
    expect(result.stderr).toContain('Unknown TEST_ENV "nowhere". Choose one of: local, ci, staging.');
  });

  test('BASE_URL beats the table, and a trailing slash is removed', () => {
    const result = spawnSync(
      process.execPath,
      ['--import', 'tsx', '-e', "import('./utils/env').then((m) => console.log(m.env.baseUrl))"],
      { env: { ...process.env, TEST_ENV: 'staging', BASE_URL: 'http://example.test:1234/' }, encoding: 'utf8' },
    );
    expect(result.stdout.trim()).toBe('http://example.test:1234');
  });
});
```

**Step 5 — see each source win.** `npx tsx -e "…"` runs one line of TypeScript. This prints the environment that was chosen:

```powershell
npx tsx -e "import { env } from './utils/env'; console.log(env.name, env.baseUrl)"
```

With nothing set:

```text
local http://localhost:8000
```

Now give it an environment variable. (PowerShell sets a variable with `$env:NAME = "value"` and removes it with `Remove-Item Env:NAME`; macOS/Linux put `NAME=value` in front of the command.)

```powershell
$env:TEST_ENV = "ci";  npx tsx -e "import { env } from './utils/env'; console.log(env.name, env.baseUrl)"
```

```text
ci http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

```powershell
$env:TEST_ENV = "staging"; $env:BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/"
npx tsx -e "import { env } from './utils/env'; console.log(env.name, env.baseUrl)"
```

```text
staging http://localhost:8001
```

`BASE_URL` beat the table (and the trailing `/` was removed). A wrong name is refused at once, with the list of valid names:

```powershell
$env:TEST_ENV = "nowhere"; npx tsx -e "import './utils/env'"
```

```text
Error: Unknown TEST_ENV "nowhere". Choose one of: local, ci, staging.
```

Clean up: `Remove-Item Env:TEST_ENV, Env:BASE_URL` (PowerShell) — or just close the terminal.

**Step 6 — run the suite.**

```powershell
npx playwright test tests/framework --project=chromium
```

### Expected output

```text

Running 3 tests using 1 worker

  ✓  1 [chromium] › tests/framework/environment.spec.ts:7:7 › Configuration › the browser is pointed at the selected environment (5ms)
  ✓  2 [chromium] › tests/framework/environment.spec.ts:12:7 › Configuration › an unknown TEST_ENV is refused with a helpful message (89ms)
  ✓  3 [chromium] › tests/framework/environment.spec.ts:21:7 › Configuration › BASE_URL beats the table, and a trailing slash is removed (99ms)

  3 passed (621ms)
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `Record<string, Environment>` | An object whose keys are any strings and whose values are `Environment`s |
| `DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT = 'local'` | What happens when nobody chooses |
| `if (existsSync('.env')) process.loadEnvFile('.env')` | Node 20.12+ reads `NAME=value` lines **without any package**. It never overwrites a variable that is already set — that is why the shell wins over `.env` |
| `const name = process.env.TEST_ENV ?? DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT` | `??` means "if missing, use this" (Lab 2.1) |
| `throw new Error('Unknown TEST_ENV …')` | **Fail fast**: a typo must stop the run at once, not quietly test the wrong server |
| `(process.env.BASE_URL ?? chosen.baseUrl).replace(/\/+$/, '')` | The override wins; trailing slashes are removed so `baseUrl + '/x'` never has `//` |
| `testUserPassword: process.env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD \|\| \`Pw-…\`` | A password from the environment, or a random one for this run (`\|\|` also replaces an empty string) |
| `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--import', 'tsx', '-e', …])` | Start a new Node with `tsx` loaded and run one line, with chosen variables |
| `expect(baseURL).toBe(env.baseUrl)` | The `baseURL` fixture is what Playwright's configuration set. It must equal what `env` says |

### Secrets: the three rules

1. A real password, token or key **never** appears in a committed file. `.env` is ignored by Git; `.env.example` shows only the **names**.
2. A CI server stores secrets in its own secret store and passes them as environment variables.
3. A test must not print a secret. (The random password is built per run and never logged.)

### Common mistakes

* **Committing `.env`.** Check `git status` before every commit; `.env` must not be listed.
* **Reading `process.env` in many files.** Then no one knows what the suite depends on. Only `utils/env.ts` reads it.
* **A typo in `TEST_ENV` silently falling back to `local`.** Our module throws instead — keep it that way.
* **A hard-coded URL in a test** (`page.goto('http://localhost:8000/login/')`). Use a path (`'/login/'`) and let `baseURL` supply the rest.
* **Pointing a destructive test at a shared environment** without thinking. Staging data belongs to other people. Tests that create data need unique names (Lab 5.5) and, in Phase 6, cleanup.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Unknown TEST_ENV "…". Choose one of: local, ci, staging.` | A misspelt name | Use one of the listed names, or add one to the table |
| `.env` seems ignored | A real variable with the same name is set in the shell | The shell wins by design; remove the variable |
| `.env` values have quotes in the test | Quotes are part of the value in some loaders | Write `NAME=value` without quotes |
| Run against `staging` fails with `ENOTFOUND` | The staging host in the table is a placeholder | Replace it with your real address, or use `BASE_URL` |
| Windows: `TEST_ENV=ci npx …` is "not recognised" | That syntax is for macOS/Linux | PowerShell: `$env:TEST_ENV = "ci"` first |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Add a fourth environment, `docker`, at `http://localhost:8080`, and prove it is selected with `TEST_ENV=docker`.
2. Make the run print which environment it will test (this is what the next lab's global set-up does). Where would you put the line, and why not in every test?
3. Explain why `TEST_USER_PASSWORD` is not in `config/environments.ts` even though it is configuration.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

1. ```ts
   docker: { baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080', description: 'the app in a container' },
   ```
   then `TEST_ENV=docker npx tsx -e "import { env } from './utils/env'; console.log(env.name, env.baseUrl)"` prints `docker http://localhost:8080`.
2. In `global-setup.ts` (Lab 5.7): it runs once per run. In a test it would print hundreds of times.
3. `config/environments.ts` is committed to Git, and a password is a secret. Secrets come from the environment only.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 5.6)

1. Which wins: a variable set in the shell or a line in `.env`? *(The shell variable.)*
2. What is a base URL and why is it not written in tests? *(The shared start of every address; tests use paths so the same test runs in any environment.)*
3. What does "fail fast" mean for `TEST_ENV`? *(An unknown name stops the run immediately with a helpful message.)*
4. What is the difference between `.env` and `.env.example`? *(`.env` holds your real values and is never committed; the example shows names only and is committed.)*

- [ ] I saw `BASE_URL` override and an unknown `TEST_ENV` refused.
- [ ] `.env` is not tracked by Git (`git status` does not list it).
- [ ] `environment.spec.ts` passes.

## Lab 5.7 — Authentication set-up, global set-up and tear-down 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Compare the **three ways** a test can be signed in, and choose between them.
* Rewrite the saved-session set-up (Lab 4.6) with page objects.
* Add a **global set-up** that stops the run early when the application is unreachable.
* Add a **tear-down** that removes the saved session file after the run.

### Concepts in simple language

You can now sign a user in in three ways. Each has a price:

| Way | How | Speed | Isolation | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Per test** | The `registeredUser` + `booksPage` fixtures (Lab 5.4) | ≈ 1–2 s per test | Best: a new user every test | The test changes the user's data, or tests sign-in itself |
| **Saved session** | The `setup` project saves `storageState`; the `chromium-auth` project starts signed in (Lab 4.6) | Fastest | One user **shared** by many tests; no sign-out tests | Read-mostly tests (searching, viewing, mocking) |
| **By API** | An API call creates the session | Fast **and** isolated | Best of both | Phase 6 |

**Three places to run code once, before or after tests** — they are easy to confuse:

| Tool | Runs | Appears in the report? | Gets fixtures (`page`…)? | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fixture** with `use()` | around **every test** that asks | inside the test | yes | per-test set-up and clean-up |
| **Setup project** (`auth.setup.ts`) with `dependencies` | once, **before** the projects that need it | yes, as tests | yes | signing in and saving state |
| **Teardown project** (`teardown: 'cleanup'`) | once, **after** those projects | yes | yes | deleting what set-up created |
| **`globalSetup`** file | once, before **everything** | no (only the console) | no | fast checks: "is the server up?", create a folder |

Playwright's advice: for signing in, prefer **project dependencies** (they produce traces and reports); keep `globalSetup` for small non-browser checks.

**Why remove the saved session?** `.auth/user.json` is a **live session key**. Leaving it on disk after the run is leaving a key under the mat. A teardown deletes it. When *you* want to inspect it (Lab 4.6), run with `KEEP_AUTH=1`.

### Why QA needs it

Signing in is the most repeated step in a suite. Done badly it makes the suite slow and flaky; done well it is invisible. And a run that goes against a server that is not even running should fail in **two seconds with a clear sentence**, not after 40 tests each waited 30 seconds.

### Prerequisites

Labs 5.1–5.6; Lab 4.6 (`storageState`).

### Files

```
global-setup.ts                          NEW  the reachability check
tests/cleanup.teardown.ts                NEW  removes .auth after the run
tests/auth.setup.ts                      CHANGED  uses page objects
playwright.config.ts                     CHANGED  globalSetup + the cleanup project
tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts   NEW  a saved-session test written with a page object
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the global set-up.** Create `global-setup.ts` in the `e2e` folder. It asks the application's health address and, if that fails, stops the whole run with a message that says what to do:

*File: `e2e/global-setup.ts`*

```ts
import { env } from './utils/env';

/**
 * Runs ONCE, before any test or project. Use it for checks that make the whole run pointless
 * if they fail. Here: is the application reachable? A clear message in two seconds beats
 * 40 tests that each wait 30 seconds and then fail with "net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED".
 */
export default async function globalSetup(): Promise<void> {
  const url = `${env.baseUrl}/api/health/`;
  try {
    const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) });
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`answered with HTTP ${response.status}`);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error(
      `The application is not reachable at ${env.baseUrl} (${env.name}: ${env.description}).\n` +
        `  Tried: ${url}\n  Problem: ${(error as Error).message}\n` +
        `  Start the application, or choose another environment with TEST_ENV or BASE_URL.`,
    );
  }
  console.log(`Testing ${env.baseUrl}  [${env.name}: ${env.description}]`);
}
```

**Step 2 — the teardown.** Create `tests/cleanup.teardown.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/cleanup.teardown.ts`*

```ts
import { test as teardown } from '@playwright/test';
import { rmSync } from 'node:fs';

/**
 * Runs ONCE after every project that depends on `setup` has finished.
 * The saved sign-in file is a live session key, so we do not leave it lying around.
 * Set KEEP_AUTH=1 when you want to look at it (Lab 4.6).
 */
teardown('remove the saved sign-in state', async () => {
  if (process.env.KEEP_AUTH === '1') return;
  rmSync('.auth', { recursive: true, force: true });
});
```

**Step 3 — the sign-in set-up with page objects.** Replace `tests/auth.setup.ts`. Compare it with Lab 4.6: the nine lines of locators have become three lines of intent.

*File: `e2e/tests/auth.setup.ts`*

```ts
import { test as setup } from '@playwright/test';
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { LoginPage, RegisterPage } from '../pages';
import { makeUser } from '../data/users';

const STATE_FILE = '.auth/user.json'; // cookies + local storage of the signed-in browser
const USER_FILE = '.auth/user-info.json'; // who that user is (tests need the name)

setup('create a user, sign in once, save the state', async ({ page }) => {
  const user = makeUser('stored');

  const register = new RegisterPage(page);
  await register.open();
  await register.registerAs(user);

  const login = new LoginPage(page);
  await login.signInAs(user);

  mkdirSync('.auth', { recursive: true });
  await page.context().storageState({ path: STATE_FILE });
  writeFileSync(USER_FILE, JSON.stringify({ username: user.username }));
});
```

**Step 4 — the configuration.** Replace `playwright.config.ts`. Two things are new: the `globalSetup` line and the `cleanup` project, which the `setup` project names as its `teardown`.

*File: `e2e/playwright.config.ts`*

```ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';
import { env } from './utils/env';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './tests',
  globalSetup: './global-setup',   // Lab 5.7: is the application reachable?
  timeout: 30_000,
  expect: { timeout: 5_000 },
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: 0,                    // see Lab 4.9 for when (and when not) to retry
  reporter: [['list'], ['html', { open: 'never' }]],

  use: {
    baseURL: env.baseUrl,
    headless: process.env.HEADED !== '1',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
    video: 'retain-on-failure',  // NEW in Phase 4: a short film of a failed test
  },

  projects: [
    // 1) Runs first, once: signs in and saves the browser's sign-in state to a file.
    { name: 'setup', testMatch: /.*\.setup\.ts/, teardown: 'cleanup' },

    // 1b) Runs last, once: removes the saved sign-in file (Lab 5.7).
    { name: 'cleanup', testMatch: /.*\.teardown\.ts/ },

    // 2) The tests from Phase 3 and the "advanced" tests: every test signs in for itself.
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      testIgnore: [/\/auth\//],
    },

    // 3) Tests that start ALREADY signed in, using the saved state (Lab 4.6).
    {
      name: 'chromium-auth',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], storageState: '.auth/user.json' },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
      testMatch: /\/auth\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
    },
  ],
});
```

**Step 5 — a saved-session test with a page object.** Create `tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import { BooksPage } from '../../pages';
import { storedUsername } from '../../utils/auth-state';

test('a saved session opens the Books page through its page object', async ({ page }) => {
  const booksPage = new BooksPage(page);
  await booksPage.open(); // no sign-in steps: the project supplies the saved state
  await booksPage.header.expectSignedInAs(storedUsername());
});
```

**Step 6 — run the saved-session tests.** Playwright runs `setup` first because `chromium-auth` depends on it, then your tests, then `cleanup`:

```powershell
npx playwright test tests/auth/01-stored-session.spec.ts tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts --project=chromium-auth
```

### Expected output

```text
Testing http://localhost:8000  [local: the app on my own computer]

Running 6 tests using 1 worker

  ✓  1 [setup] › tests/auth.setup.ts:9:6 › create a user, sign in once, save the state (1.8s)
  ✓  2 [chromium-auth] › tests/auth/01-stored-session.spec.ts:4:5 › a page opens already signed in - no login steps (378ms)
  ✓  3 [chromium-auth] › tests/auth/01-stored-session.spec.ts:10:5 › each test still gets its own context, with the same saved state (317ms)
  ✓  4 [chromium-auth] › tests/auth/01-stored-session.spec.ts:17:5 › an anonymous context can be made on purpose (326ms)
  ✓  5 [chromium-auth] › tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts:5:5 › a saved session opens the Books page through its page object (344ms)
  ✓  6 [cleanup] › tests/cleanup.teardown.ts:9:9 › remove the saved sign-in state (2ms)

  6 passed (4.8s)
```

Read the order: `[setup]` → the four tests → `[cleanup]`. The first line is printed by `global-setup.ts`.

Is the session file gone?

```powershell

Now keep it, to inspect it as in Lab 4.6, and clean up yourself afterwards:

```powershell

npx playwright test tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts --project=chromium-auth

Testing http://localhost:8000  [local: the app on my own computer]

Running 3 tests using 1 worker

  ✓  1 [setup] › tests/auth.setup.ts:9:6 › create a user, sign in once, save the state (1.8s)
  ✓  2 [chromium-auth] › tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts:5:5 › a saved session opens the Books page through its page object (355ms)
  ✓  3 [cleanup] › tests/cleanup.teardown.ts:9:9 › remove the saved sign-in state (1ms)

  3 passed (3.4s)
user-info.json

### See the global set-up fail fast

Point the run at a port where nothing listens:

```powershell
$env:BASE_URL = "http://localhost:9"
npx playwright test tests/auth/04-page-object-session.spec.ts --project=chromium-auth
Remove-Item Env:BASE_URL
```

```text
Error: The application is not reachable at http://localhost:9 (local: the app on my own computer).
  Tried: http://localhost:9/api/health/
  Problem: fetch failed
  Start the application, or choose another environment with TEST_ENV or BASE_URL.

   at ../global-setup.ts:14

  12 |     if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`answered with HTTP ${response.status}`);
  13 |   } catch (error) {
> 14 |     throw new Error(
     |           ^
  15 |       `The application is not reachable at ${env.baseUrl} (${env.name}: ${env.description}).\n` +
```

No browser started, no test waited 30 seconds. The message names the address, the environment, what was tried, and what to do.

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `export default async function globalSetup()` | Playwright calls the default export once, before everything |
| `fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) })` | Node's built-in `fetch`, abandoned after 5 seconds so a dead address cannot hang the run |
| `if (!response.ok) throw new Error('answered with HTTP …')` | An answering but unhealthy server is also a reason to stop |
| `throw new Error(…)` with the address, environment and advice | A failure message is part of the framework's usability |
| `test as setup` (in `auth.setup.ts`) | Playwright's `test` renamed, so the file reads like what it is. It is the **plain** `test`, because it does not need your fixtures |
| `register.registerAs(user)` then `login.signInAs(user)` | Two page-object calls; both wait for the next page |
| `storageState({ path })` | Save cookies and local storage (Lab 4.6) |
| `{ name: 'setup', …, teardown: 'cleanup' }` | "When `setup` and everything that depends on it are done, run the project called `cleanup`" |
| `{ name: 'cleanup', testMatch: /.*\.teardown\.ts/ }` | The project holding the tear-down test |
| `rmSync('.auth', { recursive: true, force: true })` | Delete the folder; `force` means "no error if it is not there" |
| `if (process.env.KEEP_AUTH === '1') return;` | An escape hatch for people who need to look |

### Common mistakes

* **Using `globalSetup` to sign in with a browser.** It cannot appear in the report, has no trace, and no fixtures. Use a setup project.
* **A teardown that fails and hides the real result.** Keep it tiny; use `force: true`.
* **Committing `.auth/`.** It is in `.gitignore` since Lab 3.1 — keep it there.
* **Sharing one saved session between tests that change the user's data or sign out** (Lab 4.6's hazard). Choose the per-test fixtures for those.
* **Setting `KEEP_AUTH` once and forgetting it.** Then old session files pile up.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `The application is not reachable at http://localhost:8000 …` | The server is not running, or the wrong environment is selected | Start it (`python manage.py runserver`) or check `TEST_ENV` / `BASE_URL` |
| `.auth/user.json` missing in Lab 4.6 steps | The teardown removed it after the previous run | Re-run with `KEEP_AUTH=1` |
| The `cleanup` project does not appear | The `teardown: 'cleanup'` line is missing in the `setup` project | Compare with Step 4 |
| `chromium-auth` tests start signed **out** | The `setup` project failed (see its error first) | Fix the set-up; tests that depend on it are then skipped |
| `ENOENT … .auth/user-info.json` | The tests ran in the wrong working directory | Run from the `e2e` folder |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Make the global set-up also fail when the **API** answers but `/api/me/` does **not** return 401 for an anonymous visitor (use a second `fetch`). Why is that a useful smoke check?
2. Write down, for each of these tests, which sign-in way you would use and why: *searching the list*; *editing a book*; *the Sign-in form itself*; *a screenshot of the Books page for a design review*.
3. 🏆 Add a second saved user, `.auth/other-user.json`, and a project `chromium-auth-other` that uses it. What would this make testable? (Hint: Lab 4.6.)

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

1. ```ts

   if (me.status !== 401) throw new Error(`Expected 401 for an anonymous /api/me/, got ${me.status}`);
   ```
   It proves the application's **authentication layer** is on before any test relies on it.
2. Search: saved session (read-only, fast). Edit: per-test fixture (changes data). Sign-in form: no session at all (`loginPage` fixture). Screenshot: saved session.
3. Two different people in different browser projects: permission tests such as *"user B cannot edit user A's book"* without registering twice per test.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 5.7)

1. Name the three ways to sign in and one use for each. *(Per test — data-changing tests; saved session — read-mostly tests; API — fast and isolated.)*
2. Why prefer a setup *project* to `globalSetup` for signing in? *(It appears in the report, has traces and fixtures.)*
3. What does `teardown: 'cleanup'` mean? *(Run the project `cleanup` after `setup` and everything that depends on it finishes.)*
4. Why does the suite delete `.auth/` after the run? *(The file is a live session key.)*
5. What is the benefit of a global health check? *(A clear failure in seconds instead of dozens of slow, confusing failures.)*

## Lab 5.8 — Tags, smoke and regression suites, naming conventions 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Tag tests (`@smoke`, `@regression`, area tags) and run them by tag.
* Define what **smoke** and **regression** mean for this project and keep them honest.
* Apply **naming conventions** to files, groups, tests, tags, classes, methods and fixtures.
* Add `npm` scripts so that anyone can run the right suite with one command.

### Concepts in simple language

You cannot run everything every time. A full run takes minutes now and will take an hour in a real project. So you choose **which tests** to run, depending on the question you are asking:

| Suite | Question it answers | Size | When it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Smoke** | "Is the build alive? Does the critical path work at all?" | A handful (about 10–25% here) — **under two minutes** | After every build, before anything else |
| **Regression** | "Did we break anything that used to work?" | Everything stable | Nightly, and before a release |
| *(Area tags)* | "I changed sign-in — run the sign-in tests." | Depends | While developing |

**A smoke test must be**: critical (a failure means "stop, do not test further"), fast, stable (never flaky), independent. A smoke suite that fails randomly gets ignored, and then it protects nobody.

**Tags** are words starting with `@` attached to tests. Playwright 1.42+ has a `tag` option; a tag on a `describe` applies to every test inside it:

```ts
test.describe('Sign in', { tag: ['@regression', '@auth'] }, () => {
  test('a registered user can sign in', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ … }) => { … });
});
```

and you filter by matching the **title and tags** with a regular expression:

```powershell
npx playwright test --grep @smoke                 # run these
npx playwright test --grep-invert @smoke          # run all except these
npx playwright test --grep "(?=.*@books)(?=.*@smoke)"   # both tags (AND)
npx playwright test --grep "@auth|@books"         # either tag (OR)
```

**Naming conventions** are agreements that save arguments and let you find things:

| Thing | Convention | Good | Bad |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spec file | kebab-case, the *subject*, `.spec.ts` | `books-crud.spec.ts` | `Test1.spec.ts`, `booksTests.ts` |
| `describe` | The feature or page, as a noun | `'Sign in'` | `'tests'` |
| Test title | A complete sentence: **who/what + does/shows + under which condition**; no "test that…", no ticket numbers alone | `'a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page'` | `'login test 2'` |
| Tag | lowercase, `@` prefix; suite tags (`@smoke`, `@regression`) and area tags (`@auth`, `@books`…) | `@smoke` | `@Smoke_Test_FINAL` |
| Page object class | `PascalCase` + `Page` | `BooksPage` | `books_page`, `BooksPO` |
| Component class | `PascalCase`, no suffix needed | `Header` | `HeaderComp` |
| Action method | verb phrase from the user's view | `signInAs`, `goToAddBook`, `deleteBook` | `clickBtn1` |
| Check method | `expect…` | `expectBook`, `expectFormError` | `verify`, `isOk` |
| Locator property | a noun for the thing, with its kind | `signInButton`, `usernameInput`, `rows` | `btn`, `el2` |
| Fixture | a noun, lowerCamelCase | `booksPage`, `registeredUser` | `setup1` |
| Data builder | `make…` | `makeUser`, `makeBook` | `getBook`, `createUserData` |
| Constant | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for true constants; objects like `MESSAGES` | `MAX_TITLE_LENGTH` | `maxTitleLength` |

### Why QA needs it

Without tags a team either runs everything (slow) or guesses (unsafe). With tags the same suite serves three audiences — a developer after a change, a build server after a commit, a release manager before a launch. Naming makes failures readable: a CI report that says `Sign in › a wrong password shows an error…` needs no explanation.

### Prerequisites

Labs 5.4–5.7.

### Files

```
tests/framework/*.spec.ts       CHANGED  tags added to every describe and to the smoke tests
package.json                    CHANGED  three new scripts
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the pattern, on one file.** Open `tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`. Add a `{ tag: … }` argument to the `describe` and to the tests that belong in smoke. The result:

*File: `e2e/tests/framework/sign-in.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures';
import { MESSAGES } from '../../data/messages';
import { makeUser } from '../../data/users';

test.describe('Sign in', { tag: ['@regression', '@auth'] }, () => {
  test('a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ page, loginPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    const books = await loginPage.signInAs(registeredUser);

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/books\/$/);
    await books.header.expectSignedInAs(registeredUser.username);
  });

  test('a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page', async ({ loginPage, registeredUser }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit(registeredUser.username, 'not-the-password');

    await loginPage.expectFormError(MESSAGES.signIn.invalidCredentials);
    await loginPage.expectOnThisPage();
  });

  test('an unknown user is rejected with the same message', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    const stranger = makeUser('nobody');
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.submit(stranger.username, stranger.password);

    await loginPage.expectFormError(MESSAGES.signIn.invalidCredentials);
  });

  test('both fields are required', async ({ loginPage }) => {
    await loginPage.open();
    await loginPage.signInButton.click();

    await expect(loginPage.usernameError).toHaveText(MESSAGES.signIn.usernameRequired);
    await expect(loginPage.passwordError).toHaveText(MESSAGES.signIn.passwordRequired);
  });

  test('signing out returns to Sign in with a confirmation', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ booksPage }) => {
    const loginPage = await booksPage.signOut();

    await loginPage.notice.expectMessage(MESSAGES.signIn.signedOut);
  });
});
```

**Step 2 — the same pattern on the other files.** Use this table. Every `describe` gets the tags in its column; the tests listed get `{ tag: '@smoke' }` as their **second** argument (title, then options, then the function).

| File | `describe` tags | Tests that also get `@smoke` |
|---|---|---|
| `sign-in.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@auth` | *a registered user can sign in…*; *signing out returns to Sign in…* |
| `register.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@auth` | *registering sends the new user to Sign in…* |
| `books-crud.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@books` | *an added book appears…*; *deleting a book removes it…* |
| `books-list.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@books` | *searching for a title narrows the list* |
| `book-form-validation.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@validation` | *an empty form uses the shared message texts* |
| `navigation.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@navigation` | *(none)* |
| `environment.spec.ts` | `@regression`, `@config` | *(none)* |

Tests in a loop (the data-driven ones) inherit the `describe` tags automatically.

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `test.describe('Sign in', { tag: [...] }, () => {…})` | The group's options go **between** the title and the function |
| `test('…', { tag: '@smoke' }, async (…) => {…})` | A single tag may be a string; several tags an array |
| The report line `… › Sign in › a registered user … @regression @auth @smoke` | Playwright appends the tags to the displayed title; that is what `--grep` searches |
| `--grep "(?=.*@books)(?=.*@smoke)"` | A regular expression with two **look-aheads**: "the text contains `@books` *and* contains `@smoke`" |
| `--grep-invert` | The opposite filter |
| `npm run test:smoke` | A script is a saved command; nobody needs to remember the flags |
| `--project=chromium` | Only the project whose tests sign themselves in; the saved-session project is not part of the smoke run |

### What belongs in smoke here

Look at the list: sign-in works, registration works, a book can be added, a book can be deleted, search works, an empty form is validated, sign-out works. If any of these fails, there is no point looking at sorting or edge cases. That is the test for smoke membership: **"if this fails, do we stop?"**

### Common mistakes

* **A smoke suite that grows until it takes twenty minutes.** Set a budget (here: under two minutes) and cut.
* **Tagging by hope.** A flaky test must not be smoke; fix it or remove it.
* **Typos in tags** (`@smoek`) — they silently select nothing. Always `--list` first.
* **Tags in titles** (`'login @smoke'`) instead of the `tag` option. They work, but the `tag` option is checked by TypeScript's types, shown in reports, and visible to tools.
* **Tags that overlap meaning** (`@fast`, `@quick`, `@smoke`). Fewer, well-defined tags beat many vague ones.
* **Names that describe the code, not the behaviour** (`test('clicks the button')`). A name should read as a requirement.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Error: No tests found` | The tag is misspelt, or the project does not contain those tests | `--list` and compare the tag text exactly |
| The AND filter selects everything | Missing look-ahead syntax or shell quoting | Put the pattern in double quotes (PowerShell) / single quotes (bash) |
| Phase 3/4 tests do not show up in `--grep @regression` | They are not tagged. That is intended | Tag them only if you want them in the suites |
| `unknown option` / `tag` has no effect | Playwright older than 1.42 | `npm install -D @playwright/test@latest` |
| The tag appears twice in the title | It is on both the `describe` and the test | Put suite-wide tags on the `describe` only |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Add a tag `@slow` to the test that creates three books and ordering checks (the whole `books-list.spec.ts` describe is tagged; pick the slowest test by looking at the report). Run everything **except** slow tests.
2. Write a `package.json` script `test:auth` that runs only the sign-in area, and a script `test:quick` that runs smoke **without** the `@auth` tests.
3. Rename these four bad titles so they read as requirements: `'test 1'`, `'login works'`, `'checks error'`, `'TC_042'`.
4. 🏆 A team has 400 tests and a smoke suite of 180. What is wrong, and what would you do?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

1. `test('…', { tag: '@slow' }, …)`, then `npx playwright test --grep-invert @slow --project=chromium`.
2. ```json
   "test:auth": "playwright test --grep @auth --project=chromium",
   "test:quick": "playwright test --grep @smoke --grep-invert @auth --project=chromium"
   ```
   (`--grep` and `--grep-invert` can be combined.)
3. e.g. `'a registered user can sign in and sees the Books page'`; `'a wrong password shows an error and stays on the Sign in page'`; `'an empty form shows both required-field messages and sends nothing'`; keep the ticket in an annotation: `test('…', { annotation: { type: 'ticket', description: 'TC-042' } }, …)`.
4. That is not a smoke suite, it is half the regression. Smoke should be a few dozen at most, each critical and fast. Rank the 180 by "if this fails, do we stop?" and move the rest to regression.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 5.8)

1. Define smoke and regression in one sentence each. *(Smoke: a few fast, critical, stable tests that say whether the build is alive. Regression: the broad set that shows nothing that used to work is now broken.)*
2. How do you run tests that have **both** `@books` and `@smoke`? *(`--grep "(?=.*@books)(?=.*@smoke)"`.)*
3. Why `--list` before a run? *(See exactly what the filter selects, quickly.)*
4. Give two naming rules for test titles. *(A complete sentence about behaviour; no numbering or code-speak.)*
5. Why must a smoke test never be flaky? *(People stop trusting and then ignoring it.)*

## Lab 5.9 — Refactor duplicated code; maintainability and readability 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Spot four kinds of duplication: locators, steps, data and configuration.
* Apply safe refactoring moves: *extract*, *delegate*, *rename*, *replace a literal with a name*, *delete dead code*.
* Replace the temporary helper file with a thin wrapper around the page objects, so **old tests keep working**.
* Prove the improvement with numbers and with a full green run.
* Review a test for readability.

### Concepts in simple language

**Refactoring** means changing how code is organised **without changing what it does**. Its safety net is the test suite: run it before, after every small step, and at the end. If something turns red, the last step was the problem.

**The four kinds of duplication, and the cure for each**

| Duplicated | Example you have seen | Cure |
|---|---|---|
| **Locators** | `getByLabel('Username')` in 9 files | Page object (Labs 5.1–5.3) |
| **Steps** | register → sign in → add book, typed in many tests | Fixture or page-object action (Labs 5.2, 5.4) |
| **Data / text** | `'Invalid username or password.'` in many places | `data/` (Lab 5.5) |
| **Configuration** | `http://localhost:8000` in several files | `utils/env.ts` (Lab 5.6) |

**Refactoring moves**

| Move | Meaning | Example here |
|---|---|---|
| **Extract** | Pull repeated code into a function/class | the sign-in lines → `LoginPage.signInAs` |
| **Delegate** (a *wrapper*) | Keep the old function name, make its body call the new code | `register()` in `ui-steps.ts` now calls `RegisterPage` |
| **Rename** | Give a better name | `signIn` → `signInAs` |
| **Replace literal with a name** | `'Book added.'` → `MESSAGES.book.added` | Lab 5.5 |
| **Delete** | Remove code nobody calls | the old `newUser` body (now one line) |

**Delegating is how you refactor a big suite.** You do **not** rewrite 124 old tests in one night. You make the old helpers call the new page objects, so all old tests instantly benefit and keep passing, and you migrate files one by one when you touch them.

**Readability review — five questions for any test**

1. Can I tell what it checks from the title alone?
2. Can I read the body without opening another file? (Method names are enough.)
3. Is there exactly **one reason** for it to fail?
4. Are there any literals — URLs, texts, numbers — whose meaning I must guess?
5. Would a new colleague know where to change it when the application changes?

### Why QA needs it

A suite that is not maintained decays: tests get skipped, then deleted, then ignored. The difference between a suite that lives for years and one that dies in months is almost entirely *how easy it is to change*. This lab is where you measure that, and prove it.

### Prerequisites

Labs 5.0–5.8.

### Files

```
utils/ui-steps.ts                  CHANGED  thin wrappers around the page objects
(all tests from Phases 3-4)        UNCHANGED, and still passing
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — look at the old helper file.** This is `utils/ui-steps.ts` as you wrote it in Lab 3.3. It contains its **own copy** of every locator that `LoginPage`, `RegisterPage`, `BooksPage` and `BookFormPage` now own:

*File: `e2e/utils/ui-steps.ts`*

```ts
// Small, reusable browser steps. TEMPORARY: in Phase 5 these become Page Objects.
import { expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { BookData, TestUser } from './types';
import { uniqueUsername } from './test-data';
import { env } from './env';

/** A brand-new user that no earlier run has used. */
export function newUser(prefix = 'qa'): TestUser {
  return { username: uniqueUsername(prefix), password: env.testUserPassword };
}

/** Creates the account through the Create-account page. */
export async function register(page: Page, user: TestUser): Promise<void> {
  await page.goto('/register/');
  await page.getByLabel('Username').fill(user.username);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(user.password);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login\/$/); // the page sends us to Sign in when it worked
}

/** Signs in through the Sign-in page and waits until the Books page is ready. */
export async function signIn(page: Page, user: TestUser): Promise<void> {
  await page.goto('/login/');
  await page.getByLabel('Username').fill(user.username);
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(user.password);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Books' })).toBeVisible();
}

/** Register + sign in: the usual start of a test that needs a logged-in user. */
export async function createUserAndSignIn(page: Page, prefix = 'qa'): Promise<TestUser> {
  const user = newUser(prefix);
  await register(page, user);
  await signIn(page, user);
  return user;
}

/** Adds one book through the Add-book form and waits for the Books page. */
export async function addBook(page: Page, book: BookData): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Add book' }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Title').fill(book.title);
  await page.getByLabel('Author').fill(book.author);
  if (book.published_year !== null) await page.getByLabel('Published year').fill(String(book.published_year));
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save book' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Books' })).toBeVisible();
}
```

**Step 2 — replace its body with delegation.** The names and parameters stay the same, so every old test keeps working. The file becomes a thin layer on top of the page objects, and `newUser` calls `makeUser` instead of keeping its own copy of the idea:

*File: `e2e/utils/ui-steps.ts`*

```ts
// The Phase 3-4 helper functions, now THIN WRAPPERS around the page objects (Lab 5.9).
// The old tests keep working, and the locators live in ONE place: pages/.
import { type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { BooksPage, LoginPage, RegisterPage } from '../pages';
import { makeUser } from '../data/users';
import type { BookData, TestUser } from './types';

/** A brand-new user that no earlier run has used. */
export function newUser(prefix = 'qa'): TestUser {
  return makeUser(prefix);
}

/** Creates the account through the Create-account page. */
export async function register(page: Page, user: TestUser): Promise<void> {
  const registerPage = new RegisterPage(page);
  await registerPage.open();
  await registerPage.registerAs(user);
}

/** Signs in through the Sign-in page and waits until the Books page is ready. */
export async function signIn(page: Page, user: TestUser): Promise<void> {
  const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
  await loginPage.open();
  await loginPage.signInAs(user);
}

/** Register + sign in: the usual start of a test that needs a logged-in user. */
export async function createUserAndSignIn(page: Page, prefix = 'qa'): Promise<TestUser> {
  const user = newUser(prefix);
  await register(page, user);
  await signIn(page, user);
  return user;
}

/** Adds one book through the Add-book form and waits for the Books page. */
export async function addBook(page: Page, book: BookData): Promise<void> {
  const form = await new BooksPage(page).goToAddBook();
  await form.save(book);
}
```

**Step 3 — run the whole suite.** All 167 tests (Phase 3, Phase 4 and the framework) with the application running. This takes a few minutes:

```powershell
npm run typecheck
npx playwright test
```

How to read it: the `tests` total is dominated by the **old** Phase 3–4 tests, which you did not touch. The `pages` folder now owns the locators; the new `tests/framework` files and `utils/ui-steps.ts` contain none of the duplicated ones. As you migrate old tests, the `tests` number falls and the top list shrinks.

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `export function newUser(prefix = 'qa'): TestUser { return makeUser(prefix); }` | The old name is kept; the body delegates. A **default parameter** keeps old calls without arguments valid |
| `export async function register(page, user)` | Opens the Create-account page and registers, using `RegisterPage` |
| `await new BooksPage(page).goToAddBook()` | The old `addBook` assumed the user was on the Books page; so does the wrapper |
| No `getBy…` calls remain in the file | The report confirms it |

### A refactoring protocol you can use at work

1. **Green first.** Run the tests; do not start on a red suite.
2. **One small change.** Extract one thing, rename one thing.
3. **Run.** The fastest relevant tests, not necessarily all.
4. **Green → commit** (a small commit with a clear message). **Red → undo** and try a smaller step.
5. **Run everything** at the end.

### Smells to watch for

| Smell | Fix |
|---|---|
| A test longer than ~25 lines | Extract steps into page-object actions or fixtures |
| Comments that explain *what* the code does | Rename until the code explains itself |
| The same literal in three places | A constant, a builder, or `MESSAGES` |
| A helper that "does everything" | Split by responsibility |
| A page object with assertions that decide correctness | Move the decision to the test |
| A test that needs another test to run first | Give it its own arrange step (Lab 4.9) |
| `waitForTimeout`, `first()` "to make it pass" | Find the real condition (Lab 4.0) |
| Commented-out code | Delete it; Git remembers |

### Common mistakes

* **Refactoring and changing behaviour in one step.** If a test starts failing, you cannot tell which change did it. Refactor first, change behaviour separately.
* **Refactoring with no tests.** There is no safety net.
* **Wrappers that live forever.** `ui-steps.ts` is a *bridge*. When no test imports it any more, delete the file.
* **Over-abstracting.** A page object with generic `clickElement(name)` methods is worse than the raw locators. Name things in the user's language.
* **Deleting old tests you do not understand.** Understand them first (Exercise 1).

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Old tests fail after the wrapper change | A wrapper differs from the old behaviour (a missing wait, a different page) | Compare the old and new body line by line; fix the **wrapper** |
| `Cannot find module '../pages'` from `utils/` | The barrel `pages/index.ts` is missing | Re-create it (Lab 5.2) |
| `TS2305 Module '"../pages"' has no exported member 'X'` | The barrel does not re-export that class | Add it to `pages/index.ts` |
| A circular-import crash after the change | A page object imports `utils/ui-steps.ts` (never do that: `pages` must not import helpers that import `pages`) | Page objects import only `data/`, `utils/types` and other pages |

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

1. A sample (yours may differ):

| Old file | Covered by | Decision |

| `09-dialogs.spec.ts` | `books-crud.spec.ts` (delete, cancel) — **not** the native-dialog practice page | keep the practice-page tests; they teach `page.on('dialog')` |

2. The table tests check cells, a dash for a missing year, search count text, and the header order. `BooksPage.expectRow` covers the first two; `countText` the third; the header check stays as a direct locator check because it tests the **table**, not an action.
4. `tests/auth.setup.ts` no longer uses it; the Phase 3–4 specs do. Migrating them is the remaining course-long clean-up.
</details>

2. Why delegate instead of rewriting all old tests? *(Old tests keep working immediately; migration can be gradual and safe.)*
3. Name the four kinds of duplication and a cure for each. *(Locators → page objects; steps → fixtures/actions; data → `data/`; configuration → `env.ts`.)*
4. What is the first rule before refactoring? *(Start from green: you need passing tests as a safety net.)*
5. When should a wrapper like `ui-steps.ts` be deleted? *(When nothing imports it any more.)*

## Phase 5 — Mixed knowledge check (15 questions)

Aim for **12 or more**.

1. Why are copy-pasted locators expensive, even though each copy is cheap to write?
2. Name the layers of the framework and the one thing each must not contain.
3. What are the three kinds of members of a page object?
4. Why should a page-object check take the expected value from the test?
5. Why do navigation methods return the next page object and wait for it?
6. What does `rowFor(title)` encode that a beginner would forget?
7. How is a fixture different from `beforeEach`? Give two differences.
8. What does `await use(value)` mean, and what runs after it?
9. What is an automatic fixture and what is a good use for one?
10. Name the three kinds of test data and where each lives.
11. In which order do an environment variable, the `.env` file and the built-in table apply?
12. What is the difference between a setup project, a teardown project and `globalSetup`?
13. Define smoke and regression, and give two rules for a good smoke test.
14. How do you run tests that carry **both** `@books` and `@smoke`?
15. What is refactoring, what must you have before you start, and why is delegating a good first move on a big suite?

<details><summary>Answers</summary>

1. Each application change forces edits in every copy, and one missed copy fails the build on a day when nothing is wrong.
2. tests (no locators, URLs or message literals); fixtures (no product assertions); pages (no decisions about correctness); data/config/utils (no browser actions).
3. Locators, actions, checks.
4. So the requirement stays visible in the test; the page object only knows *where* to look.
5. The compiler then guides the next step, and waiting prevents the test from racing ahead of the browser.
6. The library is shared and links overlap: find the row by a link with the **exact** title.
7. Fixtures run only when asked, give typed values, keep set-up and tear-down together, are reusable across files and can depend on each other.
8. It hands the value to the test and waits; the code after it is the tear-down.
9. `{ auto: true }`: runs for every test; e.g. failing on unexpected JavaScript errors.
10. Facts → `data/messages.ts`; unique records → builders; tables of cases → JSON.
11. Real environment variable, then `.env`, then the table chosen by `TEST_ENV`.
12. Setup project: a test that runs once **before** dependents (appears in reports, has fixtures); teardown project: the same **after** them; `globalSetup`: a plain function once before everything, no report, no fixtures.
13. Smoke: a few fast, critical, stable tests that show the build is alive; regression: the broad set showing nothing that worked is broken. A smoke test is critical, fast, stable and independent.
14. `--grep "(?=.*@books)(?=.*@smoke)"`.
15. Changing structure without changing behaviour; passing tests (a safety net); old tests keep working immediately and migration can be gradual.
</details>
