### Glossary (Phase 5)

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Framework** | An agreed organisation of test code: layers, naming, shared tools |
| **Page Object Model (POM)** | A class per page that owns its locators, actions and checks |
| **Component** | A page object for a piece shared by many pages (header, dialog) |
| **Base class / abstract class** | A parent that is never used alone and demands members from its children |
| **Fluent navigation** | Actions that return the page object of the page the user lands on |
| **Barrel file** | A file that re-exports several modules under one import path |
| **Fixture** | A named, typed, automatically built and cleaned-up thing a test can ask for |
| **Custom fixture** | A fixture you define with `test.extend` |
| **Automatic fixture** | A fixture with `{ auto: true }` that runs for every test |
| **Scope (fixture)** | How long a fixture lives: per test (default) or per worker |
| **Builder / factory** | A function that returns a fresh, unique record |
| **Magic string** | An unexplained literal (a message, a URL) written inline |
| **Environment** | A named place the application runs: local, ci, staging |
| **Base URL** | The shared start of every address; tests use paths |
| **`.env` file** | Private `NAME=value` settings for one machine; never committed |
| **Precedence** | Which source wins when a setting is given in several places |
| **Global setup** | A function run once before everything (no report, no fixtures) |
| **Teardown project** | A project that runs after the projects that depend on its setup |
| **Tag** | A word such as `@smoke` attached to tests for filtering |
| **Smoke suite** | A few critical, fast, stable tests: "is the build alive?" |
| **Regression suite** | The broad set that guards existing behaviour |
| **Refactoring** | Restructuring code without changing what it does |
| **Delegation / wrapper** | Keeping an old function name but making it call new code |
| **Code smell** | A pattern that hints at a maintainability problem |

# Phase 6 — API testing and integration

> **Time:** about 6–7 hours · **Where you work:** `e2e/` · **You will need:** Phases 1–5 complete and the application running at <http://localhost:8000>

## Phase 6 at a glance

Until now every test went through the browser. A browser test is the closest thing to a real user — and the slowest, most fragile way to check a rule or to prepare data. Behind every screen of the Book Library there is an **API**: the part that actually stores and protects the data. In this phase you test that API directly, and then you **combine** it with the UI:

* **API tests** check rules quickly (status codes, validation, permissions) without a browser.
* **API set-up** creates the users and books a UI test needs in milliseconds.
* **API checks** confirm that what the UI *did* was really stored.

```
UI test, before:   register (UI) → sign in (UI) → add 3 books (UI) → THEN test the feature
UI test, after:    register (API) → sign in (API) → add 3 books (API) → test the feature (UI) → verify (API)
```

| Lab | Topic | Type | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.0 | API fundamentals: REST, HTTP, the `request` fixture | 🧭 + ✍️ | 50 min |
| 6.1 | Write a GET API test | 🧭 + ✍️ | 40 min |
| 6.2 | Create a record using POST (and a small API client) | 🧭 + ✍️ | 75 min |
| 6.3 | Update a record using PATCH (and why PUT fails) | 🧭 + ✍️ | 40 min |
| 6.4 | Delete a record | 🧭 + ✍️ | 35 min |
| 6.5 | Validate response status and body; schema and data validation | 🧭 + ✍️ | 55 min |
| 6.6 | Create test data through the API; clean it up | 🧭 + ✍️ | 50 min |
| 6.7 | Log in through the API and reuse the authentication state | 🧭 + ✍️ | 55 min |
| 6.8 | Create a record through the API and verify it in the UI | 🧭 + ✍️ | 40 min |
| 6.9 | Update a record through the UI and validate it through the API | 🧭 + ✍️ | 50 min |

> **A note on authentication.** Many APIs use *tokens* (a long secret sent in an `Authorization: Bearer …` header). **This API uses a session cookie** (`sessionid`) plus a **CSRF token** that must be sent back in a header. Lab 6.0 explains both ideas; the tests you write use the cookie way, because that is what the Book Library does. If you meet a token API at work, the structure of your tests stays the same — only the way you build the headers changes.

> **A note on method.** As in Phase 5, every lab ends with the project compiling and its tests passing. The code in each lab is the code that existed when its output was captured.

## Lab 6.0 — API testing fundamentals: REST, HTTP and the `request` fixture 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Explain what an API is and why API tests are faster and steadier than UI tests.
* Read an HTTP **request** and **response**: method, address, query parameters, headers, body, status code.
* Choose the right **HTTP method** and **status code** family.
* Explain the two security ideas of this API: the **session cookie** and the **CSRF token**; know what a Bearer token is.
* Send your first request with Playwright's `APIRequestContext` and add an `api` project that needs no browser.

### Concepts in simple language

**An API (Application Programming Interface)** is the doorway a *program* uses to talk to the application. The Book Library pages in the browser are only one customer of that doorway; the tests can be another.

**REST** is a popular style for building such doorways. Its ideas, in plain words:

| Idea | In the Book Library |
|---|---|
| Everything is a **resource** with an address (URL) | `/api/books/` (all books), `/api/books/42/` (book 42) |
| The **method** says what to do with it | `GET` read, `POST` create, `PATCH` change a part, `DELETE` remove |
| Each request carries everything the server needs (**stateless**) | …except that "who you are" travels in a cookie |
| Data travels as **JSON** text | `{"title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert"}` |

**An HTTP request** has five parts:

```
POST /api/books/?x=1 HTTP/1.1            ← method, path, query parameters
Host: localhost:8000                      ← headers (name: value lines)
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: sessionid=...; csrftoken=...
X-CSRFToken: ...
                                          ← blank line
{"title":"Dune","author":"Frank Herbert"} ← body
```

**An HTTP response** has a **status code**, headers and a body:

```
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json
Allow: GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS

{"id":422,"title":"Dune", ...}
```

**Methods**

| Method | Meaning | Safe? (changes nothing) | Idempotent? (same result if repeated) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | Read | yes | yes |
| `POST` | Create / do something | no | **no** (twice = two books) |
| `PUT` | Replace the whole resource | no | yes |
| `PATCH` | Change part of a resource | no | usually |
| `DELETE` | Remove | no | yes (the second call finds nothing) |
| `OPTIONS` | "Which methods are allowed here?" | yes | yes |

**Status codes** — learn the families first:

| Family | Meaning | Common ones |
|---|---|---|
| **2xx** success | It worked | `200 OK`, `201 Created`, `204 No Content` |
| **3xx** redirect | Look elsewhere | `301`, `302` |
| **4xx** client error | *Your request* is wrong | `400 Bad Request` (invalid data), `401 Unauthorized` (not signed in), `403 Forbidden` (signed in but not allowed), `404 Not Found`, `405 Method Not Allowed` |
| **5xx** server error | *The server* failed | `500`, `503` — always a defect to report |

**Headers worth knowing**

| Header | Direction | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | both | The format of the body (`application/json`) |
| `Accept` | request | The format the client wants back |
| `Cookie` / `Set-Cookie` | request / response | The browser's memory of who you are |
| `X-CSRFToken` | request | The CSRF token (below) |
| `Authorization` | request | Where *token* APIs put the token: `Bearer eyJ…` |
| `Allow` | response | The methods the address supports |

**Authentication in this API — two ideas**

1. **Session cookie.** After a successful sign-in the server creates a *session* and sends back `Set-Cookie: sessionid=…`. From then on the client sends that cookie, and the server knows who it is. The cookie is `HttpOnly` (page scripts cannot read it) and `Secure`.
2. **CSRF token.** A malicious web page could make *your* browser send a request to the Book Library, and your browser would helpfully attach your cookie. To stop that, every request that **changes** something must also carry a secret value the evil page cannot read: the **CSRF token**, in the `X-CSRFToken` header. You get one from `GET /api/csrf/` — which also sets a matching `csrftoken` cookie. No token, no change.

**Bearer tokens (other APIs).** Instead of a cookie the client keeps a token string and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with every request. Everything else in this phase — methods, status codes, bodies — is identical.

**Playwright's `APIRequestContext`** sends HTTP requests without a browser. It keeps its own **cookie jar**, so after a sign-in the following requests are signed in too. You meet it in three places:

| Where | What it is |
|---|---|
| the `request` fixture | A fresh context for one test, already pointed at `baseURL` |
| `playwright.request.newContext({ baseURL })` | A new, separate context — a **second person** |
| `page.request` / `context.request` | The context of the **browser**: shares its cookies with the page |

### Why QA needs it

* **Speed:** a request takes milliseconds; a page visit takes seconds.
* **Stability:** no locators, no animations, no waiting for rendering.
* **Coverage:** rules the UI hides (permissions, validation of values the form never sends, response headers) can only be tested here.
* **Diagnosis:** when a UI test fails, a quick API call tells you whether the server or the page is to blame.

### Prerequisites

Phase 5 complete. Optional: Lab 1.5 (the request sequence of the Sign-in page).

playwright.config.ts            CHANGED  a project called `api`; the browser project ignores tests/api
package.json                    CHANGED  scripts test:api, test:integration; smoke now includes the API
tests/api/01-health.spec.ts     NEW  your first API tests
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — look at a raw request with `curl`.** `curl` is a command-line HTTP client (on Windows PowerShell use `curl.exe`, because plain `curl` is an alias for something else). `-s` is quiet, `-i` shows the response headers:

```powershell
curl.exe -si http://localhost:8000/api/health/
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 14:25:32 GMT
Server: WSGIServer/0.2 CPython/3.13.18
Content-Type: application/json
Allow: GET, OPTIONS
Content-Length: 15
Vary: Cookie
ETag: "0f0479874bf6f4a7281099b15df27c27"
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Referrer-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin

{"status":"ok"}
```

You can see the status line, the headers (`Content-Type`, `Allow`, `Vary: Cookie`, security headers) and the JSON body.

**Step 2 — see the same thing in the browser.** Open the application, press **F12**, choose **Network → Fetch/XHR**, reload the Books page and click a request such as `me/` or `books/`. The tabs **Headers**, **Payload** and **Response** show exactly the parts above. (Lab 1.5 did this for the Sign-in page.)

**Step 3 — an API project.** API tests need no browser, so they get their own project. In `playwright.config.ts` add the `api` project and make the browser project skip the API folder (the changed parts are marked):

*File: `e2e/playwright.config.ts`*

```ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';
import { env } from './utils/env';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './tests',
  globalSetup: './global-setup',   // Lab 5.7: is the application reachable?
  timeout: 30_000,
  expect: { timeout: 5_000 },
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: 0,                    // see Lab 4.9 for when (and when not) to retry
  reporter: [['list'], ['html', { open: 'never' }]],

  use: {
    baseURL: env.baseUrl,
    headless: process.env.HEADED !== '1',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    trace: 'retain-on-failure',
    video: 'retain-on-failure',  // NEW in Phase 4: a short film of a failed test
  },

  projects: [
    // 1) Runs first, once: signs in and saves the browser's sign-in state to a file.
    { name: 'setup', testMatch: /.*\.setup\.ts/, teardown: 'cleanup' },

    // 1b) Runs last, once: removes the saved sign-in file (Lab 5.7).
    { name: 'cleanup', testMatch: /.*\.teardown\.ts/ },

    // 2) The tests from Phase 3 and the "advanced" tests: every test signs in for itself.
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] },
      testIgnore: [/\/auth\//, /\/tests\/api\//],
    },

    // 2b) API tests: no browser at all, just HTTP requests (Phase 6).
    { name: 'api', testMatch: /\/tests\/api\/.*\.spec\.ts/ },

    // 3) Tests that start ALREADY signed in, using the saved state (Lab 4.6).
    {
      name: 'chromium-auth',
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], storageState: '.auth/user.json' },
      dependencies: ['setup'],
      testMatch: /\/auth\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
    },
  ],
});
```

and in `package.json` add the scripts (shown whole):

**Step 4 — your first API tests.** Create the folder `tests/api` and the file `tests/api/01-health.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/api/01-health.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('API basics', { tag: ['@regression', '@api'] }, () => {
  test('the health endpoint answers 200 with {"status":"ok"}', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/health/'); // the address is joined to baseURL

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(response.ok()).toBe(true); // ok() is true for any status 200-299
    expect(response.headers()['content-type']).toContain('application/json');
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual({ status: 'ok' });
  });

  test('an OPTIONS request lists the methods an address allows', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.fetch('/api/health/', { method: 'OPTIONS' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(response.headers()['allow']).toBe('GET, OPTIONS');
  });

  test('a method that is not allowed gets 405', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.post('/api/health/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(405);
  });

  test('a request without a session to a protected address gets 401', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/me/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(401);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual({ detail: 'Authentication credentials were not provided.' });
  });

  test('the same address can be tested with the page-less "request" in one line', async ({ request }) => {
    await expect(await request.get('/api/health/')).toBeOK(); // an assertion made for responses
  });
});
```

```powershell
npm run typecheck
npm run test:api
```

  ✓  2 [api] › tests/api/01-health.spec.ts:13:7 › API basics › an OPTIONS request lists the methods an address allows @regression @api (18ms)
  ✓  3 [api] › tests/api/01-health.spec.ts:20:7 › API basics › a method that is not allowed gets 405 @regression @api (19ms)
  ✓  4 [api] › tests/api/01-health.spec.ts:26:7 › API basics › a request without a session to a protected address gets 401 @regression @api (13ms)
  ✓  5 [api] › tests/api/01-health.spec.ts:33:7 › API basics › the same address can be tested with the page-less "request" in one line @regression @api (13ms)

  5 passed (536ms)
```

Look at the times: **milliseconds** per test. The suite never started a browser.

> **Added in Phase 7.** The order of the names inside the `Allow` header of this endpoint is **not guaranteed** — it changes when the server restarts. A test that compares the whole string passes on your computer and fails on a build server. Lab 7.10 (Case 2) shows the failure and the repair: compare the names as a sorted list.

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `async ({ request }) =>` | The built-in `request` fixture: an `APIRequestContext` for this test, with `baseURL` already applied |
| `request.get('/api/health/')` | Send a `GET`. The result is an `APIResponse` |
| `response.status()` | The status code as a number (`200`) |
| `response.ok()` | `true` for any status from 200 to 299 |
| `response.headers()` | An object of response headers; **names are lower-case** (`content-type`) |
| `await response.json()` | Parse the body as JSON (it is a promise: `await` it) |
| `.toEqual({ status: 'ok' })` | Deep comparison of the whole object |
| `request.fetch(path, { method: 'OPTIONS' })` | The general call, for methods that have no shortcut |
| `request.post('/api/health/')` | The health address allows only `GET`; the server answers `405` |
| `await expect(response).toBeOK()` | An assertion made for responses: passes for 2xx and prints status and body when it fails |
| `project 'api'` with `testMatch` | Only files under `tests/api/`; no `devices`, no browser |
| `testIgnore: [/\/auth\//, /\/tests\/api\//]` | The browser project must not run API tests too |
| `--project=chromium --project=api` in `test:smoke` | The smoke suite now covers both layers |

### See what a failing response assertion tells you

Try to expect "OK" from a protected address while signed out. This temporary test:

*File: `e2e/tests/api/zz-tobeok.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('expects the protected address to be OK without signing in', async ({ request }) => {
  const response = await request.get('/api/me/');
  await expect(response).toBeOK();
});
```

fails with a message that already contains the answer:

```text
  1) [api] › tests/api/zz-tobeok.spec.ts:3:5 › expects the protected address to be OK without signing in 

    Error: expect(response).toBeOK() failed

    Call log:
    → GET http://localhost:8000/api/me/
      user-agent: Playwright/1.63.0 (x64; ubuntu 24.04) node/22.23
      accept: */*
      accept-encoding: gzip,deflate,br
    ← 401 Unauthorized
      date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 14:25:34 GMT
      server: WSGIServer/0.2 CPython/3.13.18
      content-type: application/json
      www-authenticate: Session
      allow: GET, OPTIONS
```

(Do not keep this file. `toBeOK()` is excellent when you want "any success"; use `expect(response.status()).toBe(200)` when you want a **specific** code — a `201` is also "OK".)

### Common mistakes

* **Forgetting `await`** on `request.get(...)` or `response.json()`. You then compare a Promise with an object.
* **Asserting only `ok()`** when the requirement is a specific status (`201` for create, `204` for delete).
* **Reading headers with capital letters** (`headers()['Content-Type']` is `undefined`). Use lower case.
* **Using `curl` in PowerShell** without `.exe`.
* **Running API tests in the browser project** — they would pass, but start a browser for nothing.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8000` / the global set-up message from Lab 5.7 | The application is not running | Start it (`python manage.py runserver`) |
| `apiRequestContext.get: Invalid URL` | No `baseURL` and a path without host | Run through the Playwright config (`baseURL` comes from `utils/env.ts`) |
| Tests run but a browser window flashes | The test file imports `test` from `fixtures` (which has the `page` fixtures) | API-only specs import from `'../../fixtures/api'` (Lab 6.2) or `@playwright/test` |
| `expect(received).toEqual(expected)` on JSON | A field was added to the response | Decide: is the new field part of the contract? Update the test deliberately |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. With `curl.exe -si`, request `http://localhost:8000/api/me/` and `http://localhost:8000/api/books/0/`. Write down the status line and the body of each, and say which status family each belongs to and **why**.
2. Add a test to `01-health.spec.ts`: `GET /api/csrf/` returns `200` and a JSON body with a non-empty `csrfToken` string, and the response sets a cookie (`set-cookie` header contains `csrftoken`).
3. Classify with the table in *Concepts*: (a) a login with a wrong password → ?; (b) a signed-in user deleting somebody else's book → ?; (c) creating a book without a title → ?; (d) the server's database is down → ?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

1. `/api/me/` → `401 Unauthorized`, `{"detail":"Authentication credentials were not provided."}` (4xx: you did not identify yourself). `/api/books/0/` → `404 Not Found`, `{"detail":"No Book matches the given query."}` (4xx: the resource does not exist).
2. ```ts
   test('the CSRF endpoint hands out a token and sets the cookie', async ({ request }) => {
     const response = await request.get('/api/csrf/');
     expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
     const { csrfToken } = await response.json();
     expect(typeof csrfToken).toBe('string');
     expect(csrfToken.length).toBeGreaterThan(10);
     expect(response.headers()['set-cookie']).toContain('csrftoken');
   });
   ```
3. (a) 401; (b) 403; (c) 400; (d) 5xx (500/503).
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 6.0)

1. Name the five parts of an HTTP request. *(Method, address with query parameters, headers, blank line, body.)*
2. What is the difference between 401 and 403? *(401: not identified / not signed in. 403: identified but not allowed.)*
3. Which method is not idempotent? *(POST — repeating it creates another record.)*
4. What does the CSRF token protect against? *(Another web page making your browser send a state-changing request with your cookie.)*
5. What is the difference between `request` and `context.request`? *(`request` has its own cookie jar; `context.request` shares the browser context's cookies.)*

## Lab 6.1 — Write a GET API test 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Test a **read** endpoint: status, headers, body structure.
* Use **query parameters** (`search`, `ordering`) through the `params` option.
* Test the **not found** and **unknown address** cases.
* Write assertions that stay true on a **shared, changing** library.

### Concepts in simple language

`GET /api/books/` returns the list of all books. It needs **no sign-in** — reading is public — and accepts optional **query parameters**:

| Parameter | Effect | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `search` | Case-insensitive match in title **or** author | `?search=dune` |
| `ordering` | Sort order; a minus sign reverses it. Unknown values are ignored | `?ordering=-id` |

`GET /api/books/{id}/` returns one book, or `404`.

**What to check in a GET test**

| Layer | Example |
|---|---|
| Status | `200` |
| Headers | `content-type` is JSON |
| Body shape | a list; every item has the six fields |
| Body data | ordering really orders; a search that matches nothing gives `[]` |
| Error cases | a missing book gives `404` with an explanation |

**A shared library is a trap.** The application contains books made by everyone — this very course has already added hundreds. A test must not say "there are 3 books". It can say "if I ask for ids in descending order, the ids I get are in descending order", which is true whatever the books are.

### Why QA needs it

GET tests are the safest API tests: they change nothing, so they can run anywhere, even against production-like systems, and they find many defects (wrong status for an empty result, wrong sort, leaking fields).

### Prerequisites

Lab 6.0.

### Files

```
tests/api/02-get-books.spec.ts      NEW  ten read tests
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the tests.** Create `tests/api/02-get-books.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/api/02-get-books.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { uid } from '../../utils/test-data';
import type { Book } from '../../utils/types';

// Lab 6.1: raw `request` calls. (Lab 6.2 introduces a small client class that shortens them.)
test.describe('GET /api/books/', { tag: ['@regression', '@api'] }, () => {
  test('anyone can read the list: 200, JSON, a list', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/books/'); // no sign-in needed to READ

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(response.headers()['content-type']).toContain('application/json');
    expect(Array.isArray(await response.json())).toBe(true);
  });

  test('every book has exactly the six documented fields', async ({ request }) => {
    const books = (await (await request.get('/api/books/')).json()) as Book[];

    for (const book of books.slice(0, 20)) {
      expect(Object.keys(book).sort()).toEqual(['author', 'created_at', 'id', 'owner', 'published_year', 'title']);
    }
  });

  test('ordering by id works in both directions', async ({ request }) => {
    const ids = async (ordering: string) =>
      ((await (await request.get('/api/books/', { params: { ordering } })).json()) as Book[]).map((b) => b.id);
    const ascending = await ids('id');
    const descending = await ids('-id');

    expect(ascending).toEqual([...ascending].sort((a, b) => a - b));
    expect(descending).toEqual([...descending].sort((a, b) => b - a));
  });

  test('a search that matches nothing returns an empty list, not an error', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/books/', { params: { search: `nothing-${uid()}` } });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('an unknown ordering value is ignored', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/books/', { params: { ordering: 'colour' } });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
  });

  test('query parameters travel in the address', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/books/', { params: { search: 'war and peace', ordering: '-id' } });
    const url = new URL(response.url());

    expect(url.pathname).toBe('/api/books/');
    expect(url.searchParams.get('search')).toBe('war and peace'); // spaces were encoded for us
    expect(url.searchParams.get('ordering')).toBe('-id');
  });

  test('one book can be read by its id', async ({ request }) => {
    const books = (await (await request.get('/api/books/')).json()) as Book[];
    test.skip(books.length === 0, 'the library is empty');

    const response = await request.get(`/api/books/${books[0].id}/`);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(((await response.json()) as Book).id).toBe(books[0].id);
  });

  test('a book that does not exist gets 404 with a JSON explanation', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/books/999999999/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual({ detail: 'No Book matches the given query.' });
  });

  test('an address that does not exist gets 404 as a web page, not JSON', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/nothing-here/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
    expect(response.headers()['content-type']).toContain('text/html');
  });

  test('OPTIONS shows what the list address allows', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.fetch('/api/books/', { method: 'OPTIONS' });

    expect(response.headers()['allow']).toBe('GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS');
  });
});
```

**Step 2 — run.**

```powershell
npm run test:api
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `request.get('/api/books/', { params: { ordering } })` | `params` builds the query string for you (`?ordering=id`) and encodes special characters |
| `books.slice(0, 20)` | Check only the first 20 items — enough to detect a shape problem, fast on a big library |
| `Object.keys(book).sort()` | The field names, sorted so that the comparison does not depend on order |
| `[...ids].sort((a, b) => a - b)` | A sorted **copy** (the spread `...` copies, because `sort` changes its array); the numeric comparer `a - b` is needed, or `10` would sort before `9` |
| `` `nothing-${uid()}` `` | A search text no book can contain, so `[]` is the only correct answer |
| `new URL(response.url())` | The address that was actually requested, parsed into parts |
| `url.searchParams.get('search')` | The decoded value: proves that the space was encoded and sent correctly |
| `test.skip(books.length === 0, '…')` | A test may skip itself at run time when its precondition is missing |
| `response.headers()['allow']` | The methods the address supports, as the server reports them |
| The 404 tests | A missing **book** answers JSON (`{"detail": …}`); a missing **address** answers an HTML page — different layers of the server |

### Common mistakes

* **Hard-coding data** (`expect(books).toHaveLength(3)`, `books[0].title === 'Dune'`) on a shared library.
* **Sorting strings and numbers the same way** (see the table above).
* **Comparing the whole list** between two requests: someone may add a book in between.
* **Testing only the happy path.** Empty result, unknown id and unknown address are tests too.
* **Trusting `ok()` for "not found" tests** — `ok()` is `false` for 404, but say `toBe(404)` so the test cannot pass on a 500.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Expected: [] Received: [ {…} ]` in the "matches nothing" test | The search text matches a real book | Use a random token (`uid()`) |
| The ordering test fails randomly | Another test added a book between your two requests and you compared the two lists | Check each list **against itself** (is it sorted?), as this lab does |
| `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')` | The library is empty | Add `test.skip(books.length === 0, …)` |
| `content-type` assertion fails with `application/json; charset=utf-8` | An exact match on a header that has extra parts | Use `toContain('application/json')` |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Add a test: `?ordering=published_year` returns books whose non-null years never decrease. (Filter out `null` first. What did you learn about nulls from the UI sort test of Lab 3.7?)
2. Add a test that `GET /api/books/?search=` (empty search) returns the same **kind** of answer as no parameter (200, a list).
3. Write down three more GET scenarios you would test on this endpoint, and one thing you would *not* test and why.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

```ts
// 1
test('ordering by year never decreases', async ({ request }) => {
  const books = (await (await request.get('/api/books/', { params: { ordering: 'published_year' } })).json()) as Book[];
  const years = books.map((b) => b.published_year).filter((y): y is number => y !== null);
  expect(years).toEqual([...years].sort((a, b) => a - b));
});
```
The `filter((y): y is number => …)` is a **type guard** that tells TypeScript the nulls are gone. Nulls are placed first or last by the database, which is why they are filtered out.

2 — `request.get('/api/books/', { params: { search: '' } })` → 200 and an array.

3 — Examples: search is case-insensitive; search matches the author as well as the title; combining `search` and `ordering`; the response does not include fields it should not. Not tested: the exact number or order of books in the shared library.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 6.1)

1. Does reading the list require signing in? *(No.)*
2. Why is `params: {…}` better than building the address with `+`? *(It encodes special characters and avoids typos.)*
3. Why must a GET test on a shared library avoid exact counts? *(Other tests and users add and remove books.)*
4. What differs between the 404 of a missing book and of a missing address? *(JSON `{"detail":…}` vs an HTML page.)*

## Lab 6.2 — Create a record using POST (and a small API client) 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Register and sign in through the API, including the **CSRF** handshake.
* Create a book with `POST` and check `201`, the stored record and the server-set **owner**.
* Test the failure cases: `400` validation, `401` anonymous, `403` forbidden/CSRF.
* Wrap the handshake in a small, typed **client class** and **fixtures**, so tests stay short.

### Concepts in simple language

Changing data needs three things the GET tests did not:

1. **Who you are** — register once, then sign in (`POST /api/register/`, `POST /api/login/`).
2. **The CSRF token** — fetch it (`GET /api/csrf/`) and send it in `X-CSRFToken` on every `POST`.
3. **A body** — `request.post(path, { data: { … } })`; Playwright sets `Content-Type: application/json` for you.

Doing this by hand in every test would bury the idea under plumbing. The remedy is the Phase 5 idea again: **put the know-how in one class**. `ApiClient` is a "page object for the API": it knows *how* to talk to the server, tests say *what* should happen.

**Two kinds of methods — a design you will reuse**

| Kind | Name | Returns | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Raw** | `createBookRaw(data)` | the whole `APIResponse` | tests that check **any** status (`400`, `403`…) |
| **Checked** | `createBook(book)` | the typed `Book` | **arranging** data: it asserts `201` and fails with the server's own message if not |

**Two people = two clients.** A client owns one cookie jar. For a second person (an owner and a stranger) make a second context.

**What POST should answer**

| Situation | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Valid data | `201 Created` | The stored record, with `id`, `owner`, `created_at` |
| Invalid data | `400 Bad Request` | `{ "field": ["message", …] }` |
| Not signed in | `401 Unauthorized` | `{ "detail": "…" }` |
| Signed in, no CSRF header | `403 Forbidden` | `{ "detail": "CSRF Failed: …" }` |

### Why QA needs it

Creating records is where most business rules live: validation, ownership, trimming, defaults. And every later API and integration test needs "a signed-in user" and "a book" — this lab builds the tools for them.

### Prerequisites

Lab 6.1.

### Files

```
api/client.ts                          NEW  ApiClient
api/errors.ts                          NEW  expectFieldError, expectDetail
data/api-messages.ts                   NEW  the texts of API error bodies
fixtures/api.ts                        NEW  api, createApiUser, apiUser
tests/api/01-health.spec.ts            CHANGED  imports from fixtures/api; uses the shared texts
tests/api/02-get-books.spec.ts         CHANGED  uses the client instead of raw calls
tests/api/03-register-login.spec.ts    NEW  accounts
tests/api/04-create-book.spec.ts       NEW  POST /api/books/
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the texts of error bodies.** They differ from the UI texts (the browser says *"Title is required."*; the server says *"This field may not be blank."*), so they get their own list. Create `data/api-messages.ts`:

*File: `e2e/data/api-messages.ts`*

```ts
/**
 * The texts the API sends in its error bodies. They differ from the UI texts
 * ("Title is required." in the browser, "This field may not be blank." from the server),
 * so they live in their own list.
 */
export const API_MESSAGES = {
  notAuthenticated: 'Authentication credentials were not provided.',
  csrfCookieMissing: 'CSRF Failed: CSRF cookie not set.', // this browser/client never received a token
  csrfMissing: 'CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.', // it has the cookie but did not send the header
  notFound: 'No Book matches the given query.',
  forbidden: 'You do not have permission to perform this action.',
  invalidCredentials: 'Invalid username or password.',
  usernameTaken: 'A user with that username already exists.',
  blank: 'This field may not be blank.',
  required: 'This field is required.',
  invalidInteger: 'A valid integer is required.',
  notNegative: 'Ensure this value is greater than or equal to 0.', // the database field rejects negatives first
  yearRange: 'Year must be between 1000 and 2100.',
  methodNotAllowed: (method: string) => `Method "${method}" not allowed.`,
} as const;
```

**Step 2 — helpers for error bodies.** Create `api/errors.ts`:

*File: `e2e/api/errors.ts`*

```ts
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';

/** A field error looks like { "title": ["This field may not be blank."] }. */
export function expectFieldError(body: unknown, field: string, message: string): void {
  expect(body, 'the error body').toHaveProperty([field]);
  expect((body as Record<string, string[]>)[field]).toContain(message);
}

/** A general error looks like { "detail": "..." }. */
export function expectDetail(body: unknown, message: string): void {
  expect(body).toEqual({ detail: message });
}
```

**Step 3 — the client.** Create `api/client.ts`. Read it from top to bottom: the CSRF handshake is *one* private method, `send`.

*File: `e2e/api/client.ts`*

```ts
import { expect, type APIRequestContext, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';
import type { Book, BookData, TestUser } from '../utils/types';

/** What the server answers after registering or signing in. */
export interface ApiUser {
  id: number;
  username: string;
}

/**
 * A small client for the Book Library API.
 *
 * Two kinds of methods:
 *   - `...Raw` methods return the whole response, so a test can check ANY status code.
 *   - the others expect success, check the status for you and return typed data.
 *     Use them to ARRANGE (set up) things quickly.
 *
 * One client = one cookie jar = one person. Make a second client for a second person.
 */
export class ApiClient {
  constructor(readonly request: APIRequestContext) {}

  // ---- security: the CSRF token --------------------------------------------------------------

  /**
   * The server wants a token in the `X-CSRFToken` header on every request that changes
   * something (POST, PATCH, DELETE). Ask for a fresh one; the same call also sets the cookie.
   */
  async csrfHeaders(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
    const response = await this.request.get('/api/csrf/');
    expect(response.ok(), 'GET /api/csrf/ should work').toBe(true);
    const { csrfToken } = (await response.json()) as { csrfToken: string };
    return { 'X-CSRFToken': csrfToken };
  }

  private async send(
    method: 'POST' | 'PATCH' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE',
    path: string,
    data?: unknown,
    options: { csrf?: boolean } = {},
  ): Promise<APIResponse> {
    const headers = options.csrf === false ? {} : await this.csrfHeaders();
    return this.request.fetch(path, { method, data, headers });
  }

  // ---- raw calls: return the response, assert nothing ------------------------------------------

  health(): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.request.get('/api/health/');
  }

  meRaw(): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.request.get('/api/me/');
  }

  registerRaw(username: string, password: string, options?: { csrf?: boolean }): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('POST', '/api/register/', { username, password }, options);
  }

  loginRaw(username: string, password: string, options?: { csrf?: boolean }): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('POST', '/api/login/', { username, password }, options);
  }

  logoutRaw(): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('POST', '/api/logout/');
  }

  listBooksRaw(params: Record<string, string | number> = {}): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.request.get('/api/books/', { params });
  }

  getBookRaw(id: number): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.request.get(`/api/books/${id}/`);
  }

  createBookRaw(data: unknown, options?: { csrf?: boolean }): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('POST', '/api/books/', data, options);
  }

  patchBookRaw(id: number, changes: unknown, options?: { csrf?: boolean }): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('PATCH', `/api/books/${id}/`, changes, options);
  }

  putBookRaw(id: number, data: unknown): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('PUT', `/api/books/${id}/`, data);
  }

  deleteBookRaw(id: number, options?: { csrf?: boolean }): Promise<APIResponse> {
    return this.send('DELETE', `/api/books/${id}/`, undefined, options);
  }

  // ---- checked calls: expect success, return typed data -----------------------------------------

  async register(user: TestUser): Promise<ApiUser> {
    const response = await this.registerRaw(user.username, user.password);
    expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(201);
    return (await response.json()) as ApiUser;
  }

  async login(user: TestUser): Promise<ApiUser> {
    const response = await this.loginRaw(user.username, user.password);
    expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(200);
    return (await response.json()) as ApiUser;
  }

  async createBook(book: BookData): Promise<Book> {
    const response = await this.createBookRaw(book);
    expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(201);
    const created = (await response.json()) as Book;
    return created;
  }

  async getBook(id: number): Promise<Book> {
    const response = await this.getBookRaw(id);
    expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(200);
    return (await response.json()) as Book;
  }

  async deleteBook(id: number): Promise<void> {
    const response = await this.deleteBookRaw(id);
    expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(204);
  }
}
```

**Step 4 — fixtures without a browser.** Create `fixtures/api.ts`. It extends the plain `test` — **not** your Phase 5 `fixtures/index.ts`, because that one's automatic fixture needs a `page`, and a page means a browser.

*File: `e2e/fixtures/api.ts`*

```ts
import { test as base, type APIRequestContext } from '@playwright/test';
import { ApiClient, type ApiUser } from '../api/client';
import { makeUser } from '../data/users';
import type { TestUser } from '../utils/types';

/** One person talking to the API: their own cookie jar, their user, and their account. */
export interface ApiSession {
  api: ApiClient;
  user: TestUser;
  account: ApiUser;
}

interface ApiFixtures {
  /** An API client with NO session: anonymous. */
  api: ApiClient;
  /** Makes a NEW person for the API: registered, signed in, with a private cookie jar. */
  createApiUser: (prefix?: string) => Promise<ApiSession>;
  /** One registered, signed-in API user. */
  apiUser: ApiSession;
}

/** Fixtures that need NO browser. API tests import `test` from here, so no browser is started. */
export const test = base.extend<ApiFixtures>({
  api: async ({ request }, use) => {
    await use(new ApiClient(request));
  },

  createApiUser: async ({ playwright, baseURL }, use) => {
    const sessions: ApiSession[] = [];
    const contexts: APIRequestContext[] = [];
    await use(async (prefix = 'api') => {
      const context = await playwright.request.newContext({ baseURL }); // its own cookie jar
      contexts.push(context);
      const api = new ApiClient(context);
      const user = makeUser(prefix);
      const account = await api.register(user);
      await api.login(user);
      const session = { api, user, account };
      sessions.push(session);
      return session;
    });
    // TEAR-DOWN: close the contexts. (Lab 6.6 adds the book clean-up here.)
    for (const context of contexts) await context.dispose();
  },

  apiUser: async ({ createApiUser }, use) => {
    await use(await createApiUser('api'));
  },
});

export { expect } from '@playwright/test';
```

import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures/api';
import { API_MESSAGES } from '../../data/api-messages';

test.describe('API basics', { tag: ['@regression', '@api'] }, () => {
  test('the health endpoint answers 200 with {"status":"ok"}', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/health/'); // the address is joined to baseURL

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(response.ok()).toBe(true); // ok() is true for any status 200-299
    expect(response.headers()['content-type']).toContain('application/json');
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual({ status: 'ok' });
  });

  test('an OPTIONS request lists the methods an address allows', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.fetch('/api/health/', { method: 'OPTIONS' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(response.headers()['allow']).toBe('GET, OPTIONS');
  });

  test('a method that is not allowed gets 405', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.post('/api/health/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(405);
  });

  test('a request without a session to a protected address gets 401', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/me/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(401);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual({ detail: API_MESSAGES.notAuthenticated });
  });

  test('the same address can be tested with the page-less "request" in one line', async ({ request }) => {
    await expect(await request.get('/api/health/')).toBeOK(); // an assertion made for responses
  });
});

*File: `e2e/tests/api/02-get-books.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures/api';
import { API_MESSAGES } from '../../data/api-messages';
import { uid } from '../../utils/test-data';
import type { Book } from '../../utils/types';

test.describe('GET /api/books/', { tag: ['@regression', '@api'] }, () => {
  test('anyone can read the list: 200, JSON, a list', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.listBooksRaw(); // no sign-in needed to READ

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(response.headers()['content-type']).toContain('application/json');
    expect(Array.isArray(await response.json())).toBe(true);
  });

  test('every book has exactly the six documented fields', async ({ api }) => {
    const books = (await (await api.listBooksRaw()).json()) as Book[];

    for (const book of books.slice(0, 20)) {
      expect(Object.keys(book).sort()).toEqual(['author', 'created_at', 'id', 'owner', 'published_year', 'title']);
    }
  });

  test('ordering by id works in both directions', async ({ api }) => {
    const ascending = ((await (await api.listBooksRaw({ ordering: 'id' })).json()) as Book[]).map((b) => b.id);
    const descending = ((await (await api.listBooksRaw({ ordering: '-id' })).json()) as Book[]).map((b) => b.id);

    expect(ascending).toEqual([...ascending].sort((a, b) => a - b));
    expect(descending).toEqual([...descending].sort((a, b) => b - a));
  });

  test('a search that matches nothing returns an empty list, not an error', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.listBooksRaw({ search: `nothing-${uid()}` });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('an unknown ordering value is ignored', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.listBooksRaw({ ordering: 'colour' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
  });

  test('query parameters travel in the address', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.listBooksRaw({ search: 'war and peace', ordering: '-id' });
    const url = new URL(response.url());

    expect(url.pathname).toBe('/api/books/');
    expect(url.searchParams.get('search')).toBe('war and peace'); // spaces were encoded for us
    expect(url.searchParams.get('ordering')).toBe('-id');
  });

  test('one book can be read by its id', async ({ api }) => {
    const books = (await (await api.listBooksRaw()).json()) as Book[];
    test.skip(books.length === 0, 'the library is empty');

    const response = await api.getBookRaw(books[0].id);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(((await response.json()) as Book).id).toBe(books[0].id);
  });

  test('a book that does not exist gets 404 with a JSON explanation', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.getBookRaw(999_999_999);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
    expect(await response.json()).toEqual({ detail: API_MESSAGES.notFound });
  });

  test('an address that does not exist gets 404 as a web page, not JSON', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.get('/api/nothing-here/');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
    expect(response.headers()['content-type']).toContain('text/html');
  });

  test('OPTIONS shows what the list address allows', async ({ request }) => {
    const response = await request.fetch('/api/books/', { method: 'OPTIONS' });

    expect(response.headers()['allow']).toBe('GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS');
  });
});
```

**Step 6 — accounts.** Create `tests/api/03-register-login.spec.ts`:

*File: `e2e/tests/api/03-register-login.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures/api';
import { API_MESSAGES } from '../../data/api-messages';
import { makeUser } from '../../data/users';
import { expectDetail, expectFieldError } from '../../api/errors';

test.describe('Accounts: register, sign in, sign out', { tag: ['@regression', '@api', '@auth'] }, () => {
  test('registering returns 201 and the new account - never the password', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();

    const response = await api.registerRaw(user.username, user.password);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    const body = await response.json();
    expect(body).toEqual({ id: expect.any(Number), username: user.username });
    expect(JSON.stringify(body)).not.toContain(user.password);
  });

  test('the same username twice is refused with 400', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    await api.register(user);

    const response = await api.registerRaw(user.username, user.password);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    expectFieldError(await response.json(), 'username', API_MESSAGES.usernameTaken);
  });

  test('a weak password is refused with 400 and the reasons', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.registerRaw(makeUser().username, '123');

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    const body = (await response.json()) as { password: string[] };
    expect(body.password).toContain('This password is too common.');
    expect(body.password.length).toBeGreaterThan(1); // several rules failed at once
  });

  test('a client that never asked for a CSRF token gets 403 "cookie not set"', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();

    const response = await api.registerRaw(user.username, user.password, { csrf: false });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(403);
    expectDetail(await response.json(), API_MESSAGES.csrfCookieMissing);
  });

  test('a client that has the cookie but sends no header gets 403 "token missing"', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    await api.csrfHeaders(); // this call makes the server set the csrftoken cookie

    const response = await api.registerRaw(user.username, user.password, { csrf: false });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(403);
    expectDetail(await response.json(), API_MESSAGES.csrfMissing);
  });

  test('signing in with the right password returns 200 and /api/me/ knows who I am', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    const account = await api.register(user);

    const login = await api.loginRaw(user.username, user.password);
    const me = await api.meRaw();

    expect(login.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(me.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(await me.json()).toEqual(account);
  });

  test('a wrong password returns 401 and the user is still anonymous', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    await api.register(user);

    const login = await api.loginRaw(user.username, 'not-the-password');

    expect(login.status()).toBe(401);
    expectDetail(await login.json(), API_MESSAGES.invalidCredentials);
    expect((await api.meRaw()).status()).toBe(401);
  });

  test('signing out returns 204 and ends the session', async ({ api }) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    await api.register(user);
    await api.login(user);

    const logout = await api.logoutRaw();

    expect(logout.status()).toBe(204);
    expect((await api.meRaw()).status()).toBe(401);
  });

  test('the session cookie is HttpOnly and Secure', async ({ api, request }) => {
    const user = makeUser();
    await api.register(user);
    await api.login(user);

    const { cookies } = await request.storageState();
    const session = cookies.find((c) => c.name === 'sessionid');

    expect(session, 'a sessionid cookie').toBeDefined();
    expect(session?.httpOnly).toBe(true); // JavaScript in the page cannot read it
    expect(session?.secure).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Step 7 — create books.** Create `tests/api/04-create-book.spec.ts`. Until Lab 6.6 each test deletes the book it made, by hand:

*File: `e2e/tests/api/04-create-book.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures/api';
import { API_MESSAGES } from '../../data/api-messages';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';
import { expectFieldError } from '../../api/errors';
import type { Book } from '../../utils/types';

test.describe('POST /api/books/', { tag: ['@regression', '@api', '@books'] }, () => {
  test('a signed-in user creates a book: 201 and the stored record', { tag: '@smoke' }, async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const book = makeBook({ published_year: 1984 });

    const response = await apiUser.api.createBookRaw(book);

    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    const created = (await response.json()) as Book;
    expect(created).toMatchObject({ ...book, owner: apiUser.user.username }); // the SERVER sets the owner
    expect(created.id).toEqual(expect.any(Number));
    await apiUser.api.deleteBookRaw(created.id); // tidy up by hand (Lab 6.6 automates this)
  });

  test('spaces around the title and author are trimmed by the server', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const book = makeBook();

    const response = await apiUser.api.createBookRaw({ ...book, title: `   ${book.title}  `, author: ` ${book.author} ` });
    const created = (await response.json()) as Book;

    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    expect(created.title).toBe(book.title);
    expect(created.author).toBe(book.author);
    await apiUser.api.deleteBookRaw(created.id); // tidy up by hand (Lab 6.6 automates this)
  });

  test('the year is optional: null is accepted', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const response = await apiUser.api.createBookRaw(makeBook({ published_year: null }));
    const created = (await response.json()) as Book;

    expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    expect(created.published_year).toBeNull();
    await apiUser.api.deleteBookRaw(created.id); // tidy up by hand (Lab 6.6 automates this)
  });

  test('a new book can be found by searching for it', async ({ apiUser, api }) => {
    const book = makeBook();
    const created = (await (await apiUser.api.createBookRaw(book)).json()) as Book;

    const found = (await (await api.listBooksRaw({ search: book.title })).json()) as Book[]; // anonymous reader

    expect(found.map((b) => b.id)).toEqual([created.id]);
    await apiUser.api.deleteBookRaw(created.id); // tidy up by hand (Lab 6.6 automates this)
  });

  test('an empty body is refused: 400 and one message per missing field', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const response = await apiUser.api.createBookRaw({});

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    const body = await response.json();
    expectFieldError(body, 'title', API_MESSAGES.required);
    expectFieldError(body, 'author', API_MESSAGES.required);
  });

  test('blank text and a year out of range are refused together', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const response = await apiUser.api.createBookRaw({ title: '   ', author: '', published_year: 5 });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    const body = await response.json();
    expectFieldError(body, 'title', API_MESSAGES.blank);
    expectFieldError(body, 'author', API_MESSAGES.blank);
    expectFieldError(body, 'published_year', API_MESSAGES.yearRange);
  });

  test('an anonymous visitor cannot create a book: 401', async ({ api }) => {
    const response = await api.createBookRaw(makeBook());

    expect(response.status()).toBe(401);
  });

  test('a signed-in user who forgets the CSRF token gets 403', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const response = await apiUser.api.createBookRaw(makeBook(), { csrf: false });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(403);
  });
});
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `csrfHeaders()` | `GET /api/csrf/` returns `{ csrfToken }` **and** sets the `csrftoken` cookie in the context's jar; we return the header to send |
| `private async send(method, path, data, { csrf })` | The one place that adds the header; `csrf: false` exists so tests can prove the server refuses requests without it |
| `this.request.fetch(path, { method, data, headers })` | The general request call; `data` is sent as JSON |
| `expect(response.status(), await response.text()).toBe(201)` | The **second argument** of `expect` is a custom message: when set-up fails, the failure shows what the **server said**, not just "400 !== 201" |
| `createApiUser` returns a **function** | A fixture can hand over a *factory*: a test calls it once per person it needs |
| `playwright.request.newContext({ baseURL })` | A new context with an empty cookie jar = a different person |
| `await context.dispose()` | Frees the context. Everything after `use()` in a fixture is tear-down |
| `expect(body).toEqual({ id: expect.any(Number), username })` | `expect.any(Number)` matches any number: we know the shape, not the id |
| `expect(JSON.stringify(body)).not.toContain(user.password)` | Security check: the password is never echoed |
| `session?.httpOnly` / `secure` | `request.storageState()` returns the cookies; the flags prove the session cookie is protected |
| *"cookie not set"* vs *"token missing"* | A client that **never** asked for a token has no cookie; one that asked but did not send the header has the cookie — the server tells them apart |
| `toMatchObject({ ...book, owner })` | The response must contain **at least** these values; extra fields (`id`, `created_at`) are fine |
| `{ ...book, title: \`   ${book.title}  \` }` | Object spread with an override: the same book with a messier title |

### Common mistakes

* **Sharing one cookie jar between two people.** With the single `request` fixture, an `apiUser`'s sign-in would also sign in the anonymous `api` client. That is why `createApiUser` makes its own context.
* **Forgetting the CSRF header** on a signed-in change (403) — or fetching a token and **never sending it**.
* **Sending form data instead of JSON.** `data: {…}` is JSON; the API expects JSON.
* **Asserting only the status.** `201` with the wrong owner is still a defect.
* **Not cleaning up** (this lab does it by hand; Lab 6.6 automates it).

### Troubleshooting

When set-up fails, the custom message shows what the server said. Using the *checked* `register` with a weak password:

*File: `e2e/tests/api/zz-weak.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test } from '../../fixtures/api';

test('registers with a password that is too weak, using the CHECKED call', async ({ api }) => {
  await api.register({ username: 'weak_user_zz', password: '123' });
});
```

```text
  1) [api] › tests/api/zz-weak.spec.ts:3:5 › registers with a password that is too weak, using the CHECKED call 

    Error: {"password":["This password is too short. It must contain at least 8 characters.","This password is too common.","This password is entirely numeric."]}

    expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

    Expected: 201
    Received: 400
```

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `403 … CSRF Failed: CSRF cookie not set.` | The client never called `GET /api/csrf/` | Use `csrfHeaders()` (the client does it for you) |
| `403 … CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.` | The cookie exists but the header was not sent | Send `X-CSRFToken` |
| `401` on a create you thought was signed in | You used `api` (anonymous) instead of `apiUser.api` | Check which client the test uses |
| `400` with `{"username":["A user with that username already exists."]}` | A fixed username | Use `makeUser()` (unique) |
| `Cannot find module '../../fixtures/api'` | The file name or folder is wrong | Check Step 4 |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Add a test to `03`: registering a username that differs only in capital letters from an existing one is refused (hint: the server compares case-insensitively).
2. Add a test to `04`: creating a book with a **title of exactly 200 characters** succeeds. (The limit is in `utils/book-rules.ts`.) Then try 201 characters and write down the message the server gives.
3. Explain in two sentences why `createBook` (checked) and `createBookRaw` both exist.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

```ts
// 1
test('usernames differ by case only: still taken', async ({ api }) => {
  const user = makeUser();
  await api.register(user);
  const response = await api.registerRaw(user.username.toUpperCase(), user.password);
  expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
  expectFieldError(await response.json(), 'username', API_MESSAGES.usernameTaken);
});
```
2 — see Lab 6.5 for the 200/201 boundary tests; the message for 201 characters is `Ensure this field has no more than 200 characters.`

3 — `createBookRaw` is for tests whose point is the **response** (any status). `createBook` is for **arranging** data: it fails loudly with the server's message when set-up itself breaks, and returns a typed `Book`, so the test body stays short.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 6.2)

1. Which three things does a signed-in change request need? *(A session, the CSRF header, a JSON body.)*
2. What status does a successful POST return and what does the body contain? *(201 and the stored record.)*
3. Why does the client have `csrf: false`? *(So tests can verify that the server refuses requests without a token.)*
4. Why does each `apiUser` have its own context? *(Its own cookie jar = its own person; otherwise sign-ins leak between clients.)*
5. What is the second argument of `expect(value, message)` for? *(A custom failure message, such as the server's response text.)*

## Lab 6.3 — Update a record using PATCH (and why PUT fails) 🧭 + ✍️

### Learning objectives

* Distinguish `PUT` (replace everything) from `PATCH` (change some fields).
* Test a partial update, clearing a field, an invalid change and read-only fields.
* Test **permissions**: owner, other user, anonymous.
* Verify "nothing changed" after a refused request.

### Concepts in simple language

| | `PUT` | `PATCH` |
|---|---|---|
| Sends | the **whole** record | only the fields to change |
| Missing fields | are reset or rejected | stay as they were |
| This API | **not offered** (405) | offered |

A refused change is only half tested if you check the status. The other half: **did the data stay the same?** After every `400`, `403`, `401` a good test reads the record again and compares it with the original.

**Who may change a book?** Only its **owner** (or staff). Others get `403`; anonymous visitors get `401`.

**Read-only fields.** The client may not choose `id`, `owner` or `created_at`. A request that includes them is *not an error* here — the server ignores them. A test documents that behaviour: nothing changed.

### Why QA needs it

Update paths are where permission and validation defects hide: *"user B can edit user A's data"* is one of the most serious defects an application can have, and the UI cannot even try it (it hides the button).

### Prerequisites

Lab 6.2.

### Files

```
tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts       NEW
```

### Step-by-step

**Step 1 — the tests.** Create `tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts`. Notice how the *arrange* part of each test is one line: `apiUser.api.createBook(...)`.

*File: `e2e/tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts`*

```ts
import { test, expect } from '../../fixtures/api';
import { API_MESSAGES } from '../../data/api-messages';
import { makeBook } from '../../utils/test-data';
import { expectDetail, expectFieldError } from '../../api/errors';
import type { Book } from '../../utils/types';

test.describe('PATCH /api/books/{id}/', { tag: ['@regression', '@api', '@books'] }, () => {
  test('PATCH changes only the fields you send', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook({ published_year: 1999 }));

    const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { title: `${original.title} (2nd ed.)` });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect((await response.json()) as Book).toEqual({ ...original, title: `${original.title} (2nd ed.)` });
  });

  test('sending null clears the year', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook({ published_year: 1999 }));

    const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { published_year: null });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
    expect(((await response.json()) as Book).published_year).toBeNull();
  });

  test('an invalid change is refused with 400 and the book stays as it was', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook());

    const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { published_year: 3000 });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
    expectFieldError(await response.json(), 'published_year', API_MESSAGES.yearRange);
    expect(await apiUser.api.getBook(original.id)).toEqual(original); // unchanged
  });

  test('the owner field cannot be changed by a client', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook());

    const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { owner: 'someone_else', id: 1 });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(200); // unknown / read-only fields are ignored...
    expect(await apiUser.api.getBook(original.id)).toEqual(original); // ...and nothing changed
  });

  test('PUT is not offered: 405 and the Allow header says what is', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook());

    const response = await apiUser.api.putBookRaw(original.id, { title: 'x', author: 'y' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(405);
    expectDetail(await response.json(), API_MESSAGES.methodNotAllowed('PUT'));
    expect(response.headers()['allow']).toBe('GET, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS');
  });

  test("another user's PATCH is refused with 403 and changes nothing", async ({ apiUser, createApiUser }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook());
    const stranger = await createApiUser('stranger');

    const response = await stranger.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { title: 'hacked' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(403);
    expectDetail(await response.json(), API_MESSAGES.forbidden);
    expect(await apiUser.api.getBook(original.id)).toEqual(original);
  });

  test('an anonymous PATCH is refused with 401', async ({ apiUser, api }) => {
    const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook());

    const response = await api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { title: 'hacked' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(401);
  });

  test('patching a book that does not exist gives 404', async ({ apiUser }) => {
    const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(999_999_999, { title: 'x' });

    expect(response.status()).toBe(404);
  });
});
```

**Step 2 — run.**

```powershell
npm run test:api
```

### Expected output

```text
Testing http://localhost:8000  [local: the app on my own computer]

Running 8 tests using 1 worker

  ✓  1 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:8:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › PATCH changes only the fields you send @regression @api @books (797ms)
  ✓  2 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:17:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › sending null clears the year @regression @api @books (769ms)
  ✓  3 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:26:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › an invalid change is refused with 400 and the book stays as it was @regression @api @books (865ms)
  ✓  4 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:36:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › the owner field cannot be changed by a client @regression @api @books (811ms)
  ✓  5 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:45:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › PUT is not offered: 405 and the Allow header says what is @regression @api @books (730ms)
  ✓  6 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:55:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › another user's PATCH is refused with 403 and changes nothing @regression @api @books (1.3s)
  ✓  7 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:66:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › an anonymous PATCH is refused with 401 @regression @api @books (700ms)
  ✓  8 [api] › tests/api/05-update-book.spec.ts:74:7 › PATCH /api/books/{id}/ › patching a book that does not exist gives 404 @regression @api @books (642ms)

  8 passed (7.2s)
```

### Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `{ ...original, title: '…' }` | The expected record: everything as before except the title |
| `toEqual({ ...original, … })` | Deep equality including `created_at` — proves that only the title changed |
| `patchBookRaw(id, { published_year: null })` | `null` means "no year" |
| `expect(await apiUser.api.getBook(id)).toEqual(original)` | After a refused request, read the record back: unchanged |
| `{ owner: 'someone_else', id: 1 }` | Read-only fields are ignored (`200`) and nothing changes |
| `putBookRaw(...)` → `405` | The detail view allows `GET, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS` |
| `methodNotAllowed('PUT')` | A function inside `API_MESSAGES` that builds the text |
| `createApiUser('stranger')` | A second person with their own session |
| `patchBookRaw(999_999_999, …)` | The numeric separator `_` is only for readability |

### Common mistakes

* **Not re-reading the record** after a refused request. A `403` that still changed the data is a severe defect, and only the re-read finds it.
* **Expecting `PUT` to work** because REST books say so. Read the contract (`OPTIONS` or the API documentation) — this API has `PATCH` only.
* **Comparing the response with a hand-typed object** that includes the changing `created_at`. Build the expectation from the original.
* **Using the same session for "owner" and "stranger".**

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `405` where you expected `200` | You used `PUT` | Use `PATCH` |
| `403` for your own book | The test used the stranger's client | Check which `ApiSession` the call uses |
| `401` for a signed-in user | The session expired or the client was never signed in | Use `apiUser` (already signed in) |
| `toEqual` fails only on `created_at` | The expectation was typed by hand | Spread the original |

### ✍️ Independent exercise

1. Add a test: patching with an **empty body** `{}` returns `200` and changes nothing.
2. Add a test: patching the **author** to a blank string gives `400` with the "may not be blank" message, and the author is unchanged.
3. 🏆 Ask `OPTIONS /api/books/{id}/` and print the body. What extra information does it give besides `Allow`?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

```ts
// 1
test('an empty PATCH changes nothing', async ({ apiUser }) => {
  const original = await apiUser.api.createBook(makeBook());
  const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, {});
  expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
  expect(await apiUser.api.getBook(original.id)).toEqual(original);
});
// 2
const response = await apiUser.api.patchBookRaw(original.id, { author: '   ' });
expect(response.status()).toBe(400);
expectFieldError(await response.json(), 'author', API_MESSAGES.blank);
expect((await apiUser.api.getBook(original.id)).author).toBe(original.author);
```
3 — A description of the resource, and the media types it `renders` and `parses` (`application/json`). Good for a quick contract check.
</details>

### Knowledge check (Lab 6.3)

1. Difference between PUT and PATCH? *(PUT replaces the whole record; PATCH changes only the fields sent.)*
2. After a refused update, what must a test check besides the status? *(That the stored record did not change.)*
3. What do 401 and 403 mean for an update? *(401: not signed in; 403: signed in but not the owner.)*
4. What happens when a client sends `owner` in a PATCH? *(It is ignored; nothing changes.)*
